utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, kindly call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, and good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-03-67-T, the Prosecutor versus Vojislav Seselj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Very well. Today is Thursday, the 8th of November, 2007. My greetings to all and everyone in the courtroom. Ms. Dahl on behalf of the Prosecution; Mr. Seselj; the court deputy; the Legal Officers; the Senior Legal Officers; and also the usher assisting; the interpreters; and the security guards. You know that today's hearing is devoted to the opening -- or the statement by the accused pursuant to Rule 84 bis. Therefore, Mr. Seselj was granted the entire day, the entire morning, that is, four hours for the purpose of his statement. But before I give him the floor, there's something to say, Ms. Dahl?

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Two points, one regarding security and the other one regarding Mr. Seselj's statement this morning. Yesterday during my opening there was an incident that I saw out of the corner of my eye that involved the security guards and persons in the public gallery having contact or some communication with Mr. Seselj, and I would like to instruct Mr. Seselj to refrain from communicating in any manner with members in the personal gallery -- I'm sorry the public gallery, be they friends or people whom he dislikes. I don't know the details of the incident, but I did see the security guards shooing someone away from inside this courtroom to people in the public gallery. The second concerns a request that Mr. Seselj be warned before he makes his statement that if he says anything that is incriminating, that the Chamber can use it against him in adjudicating this case if the Chamber credits it with probative value. Self-representation is hazardous in this respect. The accused may in presenting his defence convict himself, and I want him to be chastened that in this instance I will use what he says against him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, on the basis of what you just told me I am going to read out Rule 84 bis for everybody to understand properly, including those who follow the proceedings. 84 bis from the Rules of Procedure and Evidence: "Statement or the accused. "(A) after the opening statements of the parties or if pursuant to Rule 84 the Defence elects to defer its opening statement after the opening statement of the Prosecutor, if any, the accused may if he or she so wishes make a statement under the control of the Trial Chamber and with the agreement of the Trial Chamber. The accused shall not be compelled to make a solemn declaration and shall not be examined about the content of the statement. "(B) the Trial Chamber shall decide on the probative value, if any, of the statement." The Trial Chamber therefore concludes that the accused can speak, make a statement before -- after the opening statement of the Prosecution with the agreement of and under the control of the Trial Chamber, so it does not have to make a solemn declaration and he shall not be examined about the content of the statement. So Rule (B) states that the Trial Chamber shall decide on the probative value, if any, of the statement. So this is what sets out Rule 84 bis. Regarding this incident, indeed, I noticed yesterday that there was a security guard making some gestures, I don't know what it was. I'm sure that there's going to be a written report by the security guard to his hierarchy as to what happened. Mr. Seselj, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judges, Ms. Dahl is resorting to untruths again and inappropriate interventions just to spend my time, I believe. She was not capable of using her own four hours, she spoke for less than three hours and now she is simply envious because I am in a position to speak for four hours or perhaps even more than that. There was no incident yesterday. What happened was that a man from the public gallery was sitting here right in front of me and he was staring at me in a way that I personally considered to be provocative. Perhaps it even wasn't even provocative. What crossed my mind was that something similar happened to Viktor Korchnoi in his test match with Karpov or rather Spassky. Now, was it in the Philippines, years ago. I drew the guard's attention to that, the guard intervened, and they moved that man to another row in the public gallery. Noting else happened. I really don't see why we are turning a fly into an elephant. When the Trial Chamber or the Prosecutor are trying to violate my rights, I really know how to fight for them, and now the Prosecutor is cautioning me not to incriminate myself. I am going to talk about the facts here, regardless of whether they incriminate me or not. I do not stop at anything in terms of your views on my positions, my behaviour, my conduct over the past 15 or 20 years, I'm not interested in that. I hold the same positions today that I held 15 or 17 years ago. I have perfected them even further. However, since you have started wasting my precious time already with totally insignificant matters, I want to tell you something very significant very briefly. I established contact with my associates and they found an agency Matiko in Belgrade, a translation agency, translation for into foreign languages Proleterski Solidarnosti number 63, the telephone number is 334-1335 in Belgrade. They are in a position to translate both of my main books, the ones that I insist on up until the end of January for 25.000 euro. The price can go down 4 or 5.000 euro perhaps, if we are talking about the parts that the Prosecution already translated; that's about a third of that book, "The Ideology of Serb Nationalism," so the Registry can reduce the amount by that number of pages. So I have handled that and I hope that in the future I will not have to do the work of the Registry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you for the information relating to the translation of your book, but now you have the floor for your statement further to the Rules.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judges, I have no intention of personally hurting any of you when I say here that I am being tried by an illegal and illegitimate court. I am talking about that an institution that was unlawfully established in 1993 by the Security Council of the United Nations, in direct contravention of international customary law. The Security Council did that according to the diktat of the United States of America. During those years they were an unchallenged world power and the other permanent members of the Security Council practically carried out everything they wished without any objections. The members of the Security Council then inappropriately invoked Chapter 7 of the Charter of the United Nations speaking about the establishment and preservation of world peace or peace in certain regions. This is the first court in the history of mankind that was established as a means of attaining peace or preserving peace. So already at the outset the establishment of this court was not aimed at establishing justice, but establishing a particular type of peace, which is called Pax Americana increasingly in current political practice, on the basis of Pax Romana, the alleged peace operations of the ancient Roman Empire. This court was established unlawfully but it also has a pronounced anti-Serb orientation. Proof of that is the fact that an incredibly large number of Serbs were processed before this court in relation to members of other ethnicities. Also on a regular basis Serbs are being sentenced to far harsher sentences than Muslims, Croats, Albanians, and others. The task of this court has been carried out through many of its judgements, and that task is to falsify modern Serb history. A drastic example of this falsification of modern Serb history is the proclamation of a genocide having taken place in Srebrenica, inventing that 7 or 8.000 Muslim prisoners of war were executed there. Of course the truth is quite different. The total number of corpses found was 2500, although the entire terrain was searched, dug up, a cemetery was organized, and pedantic researchers established that out of these 2500 corpses, over 800 of them were persons who got killed on the Muslim side between 1992 and 1995 and one should take into account the fact that many Muslim soldiers got killed during the breakthrough and also in mutual conflicts between the Muslims themselves. Dutch officers and the Dutch parliament were informed that indeed a crime had happened, I'm not denying that, but 1.000 prisoners of war were executed, it's an atrocious crime but it's not genocide. However, what was done in a premeditated manner was to brand the Serb people as a genocidal people, this leading to a ruling of the International Court of Justice as well. A protected group could only be all the Muslims of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the 2.170.000 of them living there, not only the Muslims of Srebrenica. This was abuse in a premeditated fashion, that is to say a UN-protected area was abused, and it was qualified as a protected group on the basis of the convention of genocide. This trick proved to be successful in the Western media, but thanks to me and people like me this will never succeed among the Serb people. Why am I being tried here? Because I became unbearable to the Americans and to their allies in Serbia, because already in 2002, there was the danger of I and my political party toppling the puppet regime of traitors that was established after the American coup of October 2000. The Americans want to have their cronies in power so that they could obtain other anti-Serb interests, so they could take away Kosovo from us, in the future Vojvodina as well, and who knows what else after that. Now why are the Americans and their Western allies against us Serbs? Because we are a small people but a people that cannot be subjugated, because we are close to the Russians too, as allies, from a cultural point of view, from any point of view. We are originally Russians, actually, we are originally eastern Slavs, and we are not ashamed of that origin of ours, as opposed to the Catholic Slavs who renounced their origin and even agreed to go against the Russians, to become the enemies of the Russians. We did not do that. We are their allies, we are small-scale Russians in the Balkans, that is why the Americans hate us and that is why they are trying to destroy us. An indictment lacking in seriousness was issued me. Mr. President, while you were the Pre-Trial Judge, you know that on a few occasions I expressed my readiness to have a direct dialogue with the Prosecutor to deal with the some of the problematic issues in this indictment and perhaps I could even teach them how to correct some of the inaccuracies in terms of my biography; however, the Prosecutor has been shunning this for the past five years like the plague, but my only precondition was to have my associates present and to have all of this videotaped. This indictment was written in haste, it was written by legally incapable people, not exactly prone to thinking, and now I'm going to prove the ultimate incompetence of The Hague Prosecutor’s Office in this way. If we look at the first paragraph it says that from 1981 to 1984 I taught political science at Sarajevo University as an assistant lecturer. What an amazing stupidity. What goes on in your country? Can assitant lecturers give lectures on political science or any other subject? They just have classes with students. It is professors – assistant professors, associate professors, full professors, who give lectures. Even when I was expelled from the department, I held the title of research associate that was equivalent to that of assistant professor. Then in paragraph 2 the Prosecutor says that I was originally a communist. That is not true. Originally I was a baby and I became a communist when I became an adolescent, that is, when I was admitted into the communist party, I wasn't even 17-years-old. I was thrown out of the communist party in a spectacular way as soon as I ceased to be an adolescent. It was really spectacular, the way they threw me out. Now, why was that placed here at all? You know we lived under a communist regime of a totalitarian nature under Tito's dictatorship and it was customary there that young people be admitted into all political organizations led by the communist party, and when they are on the threshold of maturity, they take the best into the communist party, the best students, the best pupils, et cetera. That was the system. Marxism was the only view of the world that was allowed that could have been studied at schools, universities, et cetera. When I completed all of these schools and started thinking with my own head, I rebelled against communism. Since I did not start as a communist, I was not originally a communist but a baby. As a baby I was very troublesome. The Prosecutor had to dig far deeper into my past and to say what it is what it is I did as a baby, what I did in elementary school, and what I did as a university student, and so on and so forth. It says here that when I became critical of the communist regime in the early 1980s, I developed close relations with a group of Serb nationalists. What group of Serb nationalists? At that time there was no group of Serb nationalists. And they are trying, in a premeditated way, to find some group of Serb nationalists in the 1980s and to proclaim that that group is the root cause of all evil in the Balkans, and they're even trying to identify that group with the entire Serbian Academy of Sciences and Arts. Now, who is it that I established contact with, Ljubomir Tadic, the father of the present-day president of Serbia, Boris Tadic; also with Boris Tadic himself; also with Veselinka Zastavnikovic who was I was arrested with, she was at the time Boris Tadic's wife, and we were released from prison in 1984. I was friends with Milovan Djilas, I was friends with Nebojsa Popov, Vesna Pesic, I even went to her house, Vuk Draskovic. All of them are now notorious Serb traitors. Also I was friends with Dobrica Cosic who recently wrote in a book of his that he considers himself to be the spiritual father of Zoran Djindjic and he never said that he's a nationalist. He never said that he himself was a nationalist. None of them ever said that they were Serb nationalists. And they did not expose themselves that way. Most of them are the representatives of the so-called Praksis group of thought, these are dissidents within the Marxist view of the world. And during those years I exposed myself as a Serb nationalist and I am the only Serb intellectual who in the 1980s said of myself publicly, openly, and everywhere, that he was a Serb nationalist. That's why my books were banned, that's why I wasn't able to find a job, that's why I was restricted in various other ways. That does not mean that there were not other Serb nationalists, there were millions of people at that time who were Serb nationalists, however among the Serb intellectuals there was not a single person who was courageous to state publicly, "I am a Serb nationalist." There were not even those who were able to say of themselves, "I am anti-communist." There were no people like that. So if they criticised the communist system, they did so with the frameworks of the Marxist ideology. I am proud that for all those years I was the sole person who stated publicly, loud and clear, that I was a Serb nationalist. Why didn't others do that? Because they were afraid of the repressive measures of the communist regime. The nationalists were persecuted in the harshest manner, but I was not afraid. I am not afraid today either. I have never been afraid. I have never been afraid of anything in this world, and in my acts there were just two limitations. As Immanuel Kant would have put it, I am limited by my own internal law and the starry sky above me, the heavens. Nothing more than that. No laws, no courts, no force, no state, no international institutions, nothing can limit and restrict me, if I consider that they are behaving in an immoral way, contrary to the law and illegally, and I am proud of that. If you take a look at the indictment you can see several other very strange and ludicrous things. In point 4, for example, it says that in June 1990 I formed the Serbian Revival Movement Party -- Renewal Movement Party. That is a lie. I was never a member of the Serbian National Renewal party. Serbian National Renewal on the 6th of January, not in June 1990, but on the 6th of January 1990, Nova Pazova was organized by Vuk Draskovic with Mirko Jovic. And I was never a member of that Serbian National Renewal Party myself and that Serbian National Renewal was never renamed the Serbian Chetnik Movement and that is something that the whole of Serbia knows. Mrs. Dahl couldn't care less that in front of the whole of Serbia I have irrefutable proof that the Prosecution is lying. They don't mind about that. That's not the only lie. I'll show you many other lies. And then they go on to say that the elections in December 1990, his party won almost 100.000 votes. That is a lie. My party did not take part in the elections in 1990, it just did not take part at all. My party was called the Serbian Chetnik Movement and the communist regime which had not been reformed yet, led by Slobodan Milosevic, refused to register the Serbian Chetnik Movement as a political party. And so we were not able to take part in the elections at all, and I personally from prison - it was Milosevic's prison - that I put myself forward as candidate as president of the republic as a candidate put forward by the Group of Citizens, and I was in prison when my nomination was announced on television. And as an individual, I won 100.000 votes as one of the Group of Citizens. Now, perhaps it doesn't seem very serious to you that I insist on this because this is important for me, because it is proof that the indictment was written without any seriousness. And then it says soon after that the authorities and the SFRY banned the Serbian Chetnik Movement. That is a lie again. Never did anybody ban the Serbian Chetnik Movement. It was not banned. They just refused to register it as a political party because the Ministry of Justice said a political party of that kind with that name cannot be registered, but it continued to function and had a newspaper which was called Velika Srbija and the authorities never meddled in this and it was the Serbian authorities that had the power. Next it says in paragraph 4 of the indictment once again that after the Serbian Radical Party was founded and the Serbian Radical Party was founded with the unity of the Serbian Chetnik Movement and the National Radical party as an amalgamation on the 23rd of February, 1991, it says that at daily rallies during the election campaign I called for Serb unity and war against Serb's historic enemies, namely the populations, the ethnic Croat, Muslim, and Albanian populations within the territories of the former Yugoslavia it says here. That's an absolute lie. That was February 1991 still. I always called for the unity of Serbs, as I indeed do today, but at that time I didn't call to war and I never called anybody to war unless it was a question of defence, the defence of the Serb people. Defence from whom? From various enemies, traditional enemies, the Germans and the Vatican in the first place, and their exponents on Yugoslav territory. Because this war, the war in which we Serbs have been routed, is not a war against the Croats and the Muslims that we wage, or the Albanians for that matter but against their bosses, the Vatican, Germany, America, the North Atlantic pact and so on and so forth. And in the final stage of that war, the North Atlantic pact was directly exposed because its exponents got tired, the puppets got tired, so they had to step in. Next what is claimed here, and as they cannot ascribe a single crime to me, let alone, the heart-rendering story that we heard yesterday and I was struck by that story - if it's true, I don't know whether it is true - about a Muslim mother that was left without two children, whose two young children were allegedly killed and we heard this heart-breaking story for half an hour. So that is a true example of dirty propaganda. Where is the evidence and proof of those two children having been killed and how is that linked to me? In what way? Did I wish the war? Did I cause a war, and then that happened in the war? So how have I been brought into connection with those killings? If those killings took place and we'll see that during this trial. Now, furthermore what is used here is a whole construction. It is the joint criminal enterprise concept that is being used, and the Prosecution, in an artificial way, is linking me up with that. And then they list a whole series of names, ad hoc. Now, they've added to that list and added Radmilo Bogdanovic, who at the end of March or the beginning of April 1991 tendered his resignation as minister of the interior and from that time he did not occupy a prominent post in state power and authority, he was a deputy in parliament after that for a number of years. Then they added Milan Babic, so today it's one person, tomorrow it can be somebody else. Any enterprise was impossible in which I would take part with the persons listed. I was openly hostile to some of them, others I never met in my life, as for others again, I asked that they be replaced like Kadijevic, the then-minister of defence and so on and so forth. Now, I'm not going to tire you with long explanations as to my relationships with each of these people, I have already explained that in testifying during the Slobodan Milosevic trial and as recently you made a ruling that the entire transcript of my testimony at that trial be entered into evidence, and I did not oppose that. There's no need for me to repeat it. You have it. But I would like to refer to the construction itself. The construction of participating in a joint criminal enterprise as a form of executing a crime, a criminal act, has seem to become practice in The Hague Tribunal in practically all the trials of the accused Serbs, although there is no statutory grounds for that. The Statute of the International Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia knows of no such provision. Those people in The Hague who constructed it and promoted it in order to introduce through the JCE are the principle of objective responsibility which has long been rejected in criminal law in the civilised world. In addition to this, it serves as grounds to, through the proceedings, quite by chance, try an individual and a whole group. So through the trial of an individual, you are in fact trying a whole group. And the group does not have firm members and a firm framework. If you look at the -- it's all arbitrary. So if you look at the joint criminal enterprise in my indictment, in Martic's, Babic's, and Milosevic's indictment, this is not strictly defined because there are various names that are bandied about. For a group to be defined, a common goal is proclaimed or a common undertaking, an enterprise, and then it is being proved by the consequences of war devastation exclusively, whose tendentious identification is made in a highly selective manner and always to the detriment of the Serbs. It then appears that it was only the Serbs who committed crimes, that it was only Serbs who pilfered and plundered and destroyed and destroyed religious buildings, but crimes did happen in the war and the crimes were perpetrated by the members of all the warring sides, all the parties to the war. And all of them committed crimes of the same nature. So here all we can do is to quantify crimes and not to qualify the crimes. By falsifying historical facts and systematic manipulation with false witnesses from one judgement to another, it -- insistence is made on the fact that the Serbs are the main culprits for the war and everything that the war brought with it. What was proclaimed was that they intentionally and in a planned manner carried out war crimes in order to realise and further their own political and statehood aims, and this they say was done in such a brutal way that we have a situation in which every Serb, who in any way whatsoever took part in the Serb war effort, can quite simply be proclaimed a participant in the joint criminal enterprise. That's how far they went. As a member of this joint criminal enterprise, they can then be tried for every crime committed by the Serb side, regardless of whether that person ever heard of the crime having been committed somewhere or regardless of whether the person involved knew the perpetrators. So the perpetrators are immaterial or persons who are participants in crimes or criminal acts. The only thing that is important is that the criminals were participants of the Serb war effort even if they were highly detrimental to the Serbs. Since certain participants in the war efforts committed various crimes, then by the same token it would appear that all the other participants in the war effort are to blame, regardless of the fact that they did not agree with the crimes committed or whether they stood up to those crimes. And criminal responsibility is introduced for other peoples' conduct and behaviour with which the accused had nothing to do and from that to determining responsibility for the whole of the Serb nation is just one step away. As for this construction of the joint criminal enterprise, there is no grounds for that in international criminal law nor in national jurisdictions either. The Statute of The Hague Tribunal also does not know of this concept and it was introduced into its practice for the first time only in the Dusko Tadic judgement on the 15th of July, 1999. Afterwards, there was a lot of wavering and wondering in determining the frameworks for this joint criminal enterprise, where it was a joint intention, plan, undertaking, or whatever, which are not synonymous terms although the Trial Chambers of The Hague Tribunal tried to make them appear as being synonyms. And although the statutory norms exclusively insist on individual criminal responsibility, this artificial construction of a joint criminal enterprise introduces directly the principle of collective responsibility by which the statutory jurisdiction of the Tribunal is being expanded and the framework of the responsibilities for the accused is being enlarged. It is not necessary to prove that they, the co-perpetrators, had allegedly a joint intent by perpetrating the crime. All that is sufficient is that one of the actors in the joint criminal enterprise could have committed crimes and a participant had the consciousness of knowing of the consequences willingly took on that risk. Now, since individual criminal responsibility was not treated at the relevant time and in the relevant area, the only applicable law is Yugoslav criminal law. None of the participants who were perpetrators or collaborated in these events need not have known that there was a criminal act afoot. They did not have the consciousness of an act that was a crime. So nullum crimen sine lege is being overridden and the accused are being judged without any -- without having committed a crime. So to take on criminal proceedings and to bring people to trial depends on arbitrary choice and political needs. So with this kind of construction, instead of the rule of law, the Tribunal has demonstrated the rule of lawyers, alleged professionals who have no conscience and have allowed themselves during a criminal trial to create legal norms having the force of law, and their arbitrariness has put justice on a second level. Now, delayed justice is justice denied, and The Hague trials have been going on for a long time. Whether accused are waiting for the start of trial or for evidence or for the appeals process. The Hague judges at their own initiative expanded the notion of command responsibility, but also their own jurisdiction. They were very arrogant in explaining these actions, publicly going against their critics. And this in the face of all the criticisms. For this concept of the joint criminal enterprise to be as believable as possible, they accepted obvious falsifications and forgeries, things that have been conjured up and overexaggerated crimes. Their unilateral selection in order to cover up crimes of the war-time enemies of the Serbs and the intentions to further certain goals or reach certain goals, and this criminal adjective has been appended is seen by subsequent events. With The Hague judgements, in a premeditated and systematic and conscious manner, historical facts are being distorted and the truth, too, the truth in inverted commas, the truth is created according to the protagonist of a new world order. The historical context of the Balkan Wars and the cause and effect is something that nobody is interested in in The Hague Tribunal. The Hague judges are implementing American dictates because they are very well paid to listen and not to think or to deal with ethical problems. All the American crimes perpetrated during several military interventions by using a sophisticated air force and uranium depleted bombs are collateral damage and humanitarian realisation of supreme justice, whereas the adversaries of Americans are generic and genetic criminals. The Hague Tribunal even investigated crimes committed by the American aggression against Serbia and then they gave up the job, stating that there were not sufficient elements for criminal proceedings to be initiated. So that is proof of this Hague justice, and for this construction of the joint criminal enterprise to be applied to the Serbs, the participants in the war, systematic distortion of cause and effect in the war was carried out. Anti-Serb prejudice and stereotypes were put forward and inaugurated as a starting point of The Hague Tribunal's policies and practice and the preliminary conclusion that the Serbs are the main culprits for everything that took place.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speaker please speak more slowly. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since relevant facts are usually lacking, shameless falsification comes into play if real historical facts are in contradiction --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, could you speak more slowly, please. The interpreters have difficulty keeping up with you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will try, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, I would also like to ask you to lower your voice. I understand full well, I understand that you have a voice that carries, I also have a voice that carries, but we cannot hear the translation properly in our headsets because your voice is very loud. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will try to speak slower and less loudly, but you have to understand, Mrs. Judge, that adrenaline has been rising in me for five years and now is the day when all that pent-up adrenaline is venting. I will try, but sometimes I will forget and then you will again find me too loud. If real historical facts are in contradiction with the ideological conceptions of the creators of the new world order, then tant pis for the facts. These courts - this court does not rely either on historical facts or principles. Rules are created during trials themselves, and that reminds us of summary and special courts. This is the most striking indicator of the totalitarian pattern of legal thought dominating the overall activity of the Hague Tribunal. Although the burden of proving one’s guilt should be on the Prosecution, in practice, it is the accused who has to prove his innocence, whereas it is proclaimed that there was a joint criminal enterprise on the Serbian side and the accused is a participant in the JCE, nothing else needs to be proven. The concept of the joint criminal enterprise far overreaches the individualization of culpability and establishes the collective responsibility of the identified, quote unquote, criminal enterprise, which invariably includes the Serbian state. Every citizen of Republika Srpska or the Republic of Serbian Krajina may be indicted and convicted as a participant in the joint criminal enterprise if he had in any way, whatsoever, participated in the war effort of his own people. If he was not a traitor and if he did not serve Western secret services and their subversive activities, the legal uncertainty of accused Serbs is complete. They frequently do not know what they are accused of, nor are they capable of effectively refuting the charges. Instead of individual responsibility being established in a fully legal proceeding with equality of arms, the Hague Tribunal introduces three new forms of liability, inadmissible in modern criminal law. Objective criminal responsibility, liability by analogy, and liability based on assumed guilt. By arbitrary choice, in the selection of those who are going to be accused, the basic motives are the politial interests of the Office of the Prosecutor and its superior international factors who like to present themselves as vehicles of preserving and establishing peace. The founders of The Hague Tribunal intentionally refused to accuse or lay any charges against those who actually caused the break-up of Yugoslavia, although that was the primordial crime from which all other crimes arose. The joint criminal enterprise could only have been in the break-up of the Yugoslav state, whose international borders were guaranteed by the final act -- by the final Helsinki Act of the OSCE. Without determining the responsibility for the beginning of the civil war and without trying not only domestic perpetrators but also international ones, such as German and Vatican supporters, it is out of place to try those who opposed the unilateral breaking up of the Yugoslav state along the seams of the borders of federal units drawn at one point in time by the Communists, arbitrarily and without any legitimate legal document. The Hague Prosecutors very meticulously tried with their indictments, documents, and judgements not to interfere with the foreign policy interests of Western powers or, God forbid, their involvement in the crimes. With premeditated malice, criminal acts of groups and individuals on the Serb side are exaggerated and hypertrophied in order to lay the guilt on them from the highest political and military authorities. I prepared this to explain as clearly as I can my views on the joint criminal enterprise, as an artificial edifice. And now I will try to show you what the application of this edifice looks in practice. Mrs. Dahl spoke for slightly less than three hours, accusing me of being virtually the main culprit for the outbreak of the war because I made inflammatory speeches. But the person who is actually responsible for the beginning of the war basically participated in the joint criminal enterprise. Who is responsible for the beginning of the war? The one who tried to break up a state that had existed for almost a hundred years and that was internationally recognised. Or was it perhaps the one who tried to prevent unilateral secession by individual Yugoslav states? Which one of the two? The basic joint criminal enterprise was on the side of those who tried to break up Yugoslavia, primarily Germany and the Vatican, later joined by the USA. Yugoslavia could not have been broken up on the borders -- along the borders of federal units, those borders were installed by the communist regime. That decision, when it was made on administrative borders, it had no legitimacy, legal legitimacy. You know in the modern world legitimacy can only be established in elections, through the people’s vote, free vote, it was the communist dictatorship that established those federal units after the Second World War. Yugoslavia did not always exist from time immemorial. From the Second World War in the Balkans there were Serbia, Montenegro, the Austro-Hungarian empire and down in the south, Greece, Albania, and in the east Bulgaria and Romania. Before the First World War there was no Croatia, no Slovenia, no Bosnia and Herzegovina, no Kosovo and Metohija, no Vojvodina, and so on and so forth. Victorious Serbia, after the First World War, had within its composition Macedonia, Montenegro, and Vojvodina. And then the Serb regent Aleksandar Karadjordjevic accepted the request of the popular representation of the state of Slovenes, Croats, and Serbs to join Serbia. When Croatia was breaking up, Serb, Croat and Slovene popular representatives met in Zagreb in 1918, they declared the state of Slovenes, Croats, and Serbs, and its joining to Serbia. That state was never recognised anywhere and it lasted for a very short time, but it is a proof that Serbia existed on one side, including Macedonia and Vojvodina and Kosovo and Metohija, and on the other hand there was that state of Croats, Slovenes, and Serbs. Yugoslavia, if it was breaking up, ripping on the seams, it could not have ripped on communist borders, it could not have split again into the pre-war Serbia and the state of Croats, Slovenes, and Serbs because even in that latter one Serbs were one of the constituent state-making peoples. Serbs were united with one another and along came Croats and Slovenes. That state was proclaimed as the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats, and Slovenes. And then in 1920 -- rather, 1929, after the 6th of January coup, King Aleksandar who disbanded the parliament and political parties proclaimed the change of name to Yugoslavia. Yugoslavia was composed of nine administrative areas, not autonomous regions. Two of them were Croat, bits and pieces of others were joined in order to create the Banovina of Croatia, but they never had time enough to actually put it into a legal framework. Hitler committed an aggression against the unitary Yugoslav state. He first tried in a peaceful way to get that state to join the tripartite pact and the coalition government of the time who was made up of some Serbian and Croatian political representatives first signed that agreement, but the Serbian people came out into the street and toppled that. There was a political -- there was a coup and Hitler occupied Yugoslavia. Having occupied Yugoslavia, Hitler split its territory almost along the same borders that the Americans are dividing Yugoslavia along nowadays. The so-called Independent State of Croatia was proclaimed on the territory of today's Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and Srem; Serbia was directly under German occupation; the rest of Vojvodina was split between -- divided between Hungary and Germany. Kosovo and Metohija were joined to the greater Albania, and Macedonia was given to Bulgaria. But the seams are the same, they coincide; they are anti-Serbian. Within the Serbian people there were in the war two anti-fascist movements, one was a nationalist, the former king's army, and the other was the partisans. The Western allies supported the communist partisans, and it was only for that reason that they came out on top. And what did the Croats do? In 1941, Croats, almost down to the last man, were supporting Hitler. German papers wrote that the German army was met in Zagreb with such relish that that can only be matched by the welcome given Hitler in his birthplace in Austria. Croats were throughout the war family with Hitler, and there was even a Croat legion with 200.000 soldiers who fought for Hitler before Stalingrad and got killed almost all of them. That is the essence of the current wars of ours, our conflicts. The communists, following the tradition of the communist international agreement, formed a new project. First of all, they invented new nations to reduce the ratio of Serbs in the total population, and they found fertile ground for that in Macedonia, in which there was not particular national consciousness, the Macedonian population is something between Bulgarians and Serbs, in the east it is closer to Serbs -- sorry, in the west it was closer to Serbs, in the west [as interpreted] it was closer to Bulgarians, but there was no particular political awareness. They speak a modern Stokavian dialect which is close to Serbian. In the beginning, there was no problem with that, but the communists invented, made up, the Montenegrin nation and the Montenegrin government made people declare themselves Montenegrin. 20 years after the Second World War, the Muslim nation was invented, and Muslims were supposedly Serbs who converted to Islam during the rule of the Ottoman Empire. They took that religion and they loved it, and why wouldn't they love it because it was close to their heart. However, religion, faith, is not national identity. That's what the communists invented. Towards the end of the Second World War, the communists carried out federalisation of Yugoslavia. Since a genocide was committed against Serbs, more than a million Serbs were killed, and the most Serbs were killed by Croat fascists, clerical fascists, called Ustashas, guided by the Roman Catholic church. Roman Catholic clerics in huge numbers personally with their own hands participated in the slaughter of the Serbian people. Endless testimony exists of that. Volumes and volumes of books exist on it, and volumes and volumes of documents. I hope it is not necessary for me to give you evidence about that here. After this genocide happened, the communists tried through a policy of national reconciliation within the framework of a totalitarian regime to smooth out everything that happened in the Second World War and to form a unified state in which there would be some sort of balance between six federal units. That is how, among others, the Croatian federal unit was created, the Republic of Croatia, the Socialist Republic of Croatia, but it was constituted in such a way that Serb and Croat political leaders from that area met and agreed that the Croat federal unit should exist, but in it the Serb and Croat people would be equal and they would be constituent people. What does this status of a constituent people mean in the Yugoslav theory? That means that nobody but that people can decide on its status without the consent of that people, even if the other people is numerous, which means that the Croatians never had the constitutional right to change the status of the Croatian federal unit or the status of the Serbs within it. Maybe you never encountered in your career, in your practice so far with this problem, but I'll try to give you an example. Imagine that Mrs. Christine Dahl and I belonged to one and the same social community, and in that social community there is a prescribed way of conduct, obligations, rights, and so on. We abide by that and this community is working. Fine. At -- a disruptive factor appears, and somebody tries to change the status of the members of this community. Imagine me, I weigh 120 kilos, Mrs. Dahl, imagine, weighs 90 kilos, and imagine me saying I have then 120 votes because I have 120 kilos, and you correspondingly have 90 votes, and I thereby out-vote you and I change your status, your status is no longer the same, now you are in the minority. That is what happened in Croatia when Tudjman took power, through a unilateral act Tudjman changed the Croatian constitution, and under that new constitution Serbs were no longer a constituent nation. They were, instead, a national minority. The Serbs could not take that, and that is the cause of the war in the Croatian federal unit. Under the constitution of the former federal Yugoslavia, not a single federal unit had the right to secede. It was considered that the right to secede and to determine one's fate was exercised, used up, at the time the Federation was formed after the Second World War. It could not happen anymore. But, on the other hand, it could. Slovenia was able to secede from Yugoslavia because Slovenia does not have any unresolved internal issues, it does not have considerable ethnic groups within it. It only had to resolve the financial issues brought up by the break-up; however, Croatia could not secede from Yugoslavia and change its status without the consent of both the Croats and the Serbs living in Croatia. Had the Serbs who lived in Croatia agreed to the secession of Croatia from Yugoslavia, Croatia could have succeeded; however, without the consent of the Serbs it could not because that is how the Croatian constituent unit had been established. The Republic of Croatia, when it was established after the Second World War, was based on that principle, and that cannot be changed in a one-sided fashion by anyone. The example of Bosnia and Herzegovina is even more drastic. First of all, the communists thought that in Bosnia and Herzegovina there was a Serb majority despite of the genocide that had been carried out that Bosnia and Herzegovina should be within Serbia. And then they thought that territorially this would lead to too big a Serbia, so it's better to have a separate territorial unit. Then Bosnia and Herzegovina was constituted as a federal unit in which three peoples were equal: Serbs, Croats, and Muslims. The Muslims were not considered to be a people, a nation; they were considered to be a special ethnic group, a separate ethnic group, because as they professed the Islamic faith they had a collective awareness of their own, and that is indubitable, I am not challenging that to the present day, there is this collective consciousness based on the Islamic faith. It is not a nation, a people, but it is a separate ethnic group based on religion. These were three constituent peoples, and in the constitution it was also written that these three peoples were constituent peoples of the republic. Now, what does that mean? When their status-related issues were being resolved it was not possible to have any kind of out-voting. Bosnia and Herzegovina could secede from Yugoslavia only if the political representatives of the Serbs, Croats, and Muslims were to agree on that. From a legal point of view it was impossible for the Muslims and the Croats to reach an agreement to out-vote the Serbs and to secede in this way. Legally that was quite untenable, so that was done unlawfully and that is why the Serbs had to react. If Bosnia-Herzegovina was seceding from Yugoslavia, then the Serbs were seceding from Bosnia-Herzegovina. Why not? On the basis of what could the Muslims and Croats secede from Yugoslavia and the Serbs who lived there for centuries could not secede from Bosnia-Herzegovina, where's the logic of that? Foreign factors intervened as well. Vatican and Germany rushed in already in January 1991, as soon as the Vance plan was adopted for the Serb Krajina. They rushed into recognising the independence of Croatia. Judges, I do not have to teach you that there is a principle in international law that has been applied for a long time now when the independence of newly established states is being recognised, independence and sovereignty can be recognised only on that territory that is under the control of a central government. When the independence of Croatia was established, that recognition of independence could only apply to the territory that was under the control at that moment of the central government from Zagreb; it could not apply to other territories. Also in the case of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Independence could be recognised as well as sovereignty only in that part of the territory that was controlled by Izetbegovic's government from Sarajevo. The United Nations, according to the diktat of America trampled upon international law and they recognised states that could not have been recognised. That is what led to the bloody civil war that ensued. That civil war ended to the detriment of the Serbs then, and historically speaking that cannot last for a long time. Joint criminal enterprise, a joint criminal enterprise was organized by those who were breaking up Yugoslavia, not by us who opposed the break-up of Yugoslavia, who opposed one-sided secession. The indictment abounds in fragments stating that I advocated a Greater Serbia, that I insisted upon a Greater Serbia. And then they bring that in connection with concrete crimes. This just shows that the Prosecution does not understand the concept of a Greater Serbia. They don't know what this is all about. Judges, so far you could have assured yourselves that no one else who is accused here could have been accused of a Greater Serbia except for me. No one in the Serbian public has advocated a Greater Serbia except for the Serb Radical Party, that is our party ideology. I am the modern creator of that ideology, but that is not a new ideology, this ideology is a deeply rooted one. It's been there for over 300 years now. This ideology means that there is a unity among all Serbs. Yesterday Mrs. Dahl alleged falsely that I advocated a homogenous Greater Serbia; now, that is a lie. Intentionally when she mentioned the countries that were to be included in Greater Serbia on the basis of my speeches and our programme, she omitted intentionally when mentioning this Greater Serbia that would include Kosovo and Metohija and Vojvodina and Macedonia, Bosnia-Herzegovina, Dubrovnik, Dalmatia, Lika, Banja, Kordun, Slavonia, and Baranja. That we would have brotherly concord among orthodox Serbs, catholic Serbs, protestant Serbs and atheist Serbs. One cannot go without the other. Greater Serbia is our long-term objective. In order to attain that objective, it never crossed our mind to expel 1 million or 2 million or 3 million people, we just wanted them to become nationally aware. We wanted to convince them that they were Serbs, we wanted to prove to them that they were Serbs and others made them represent themselves in a false manner. We all speak the same language. Over here you call that language inappropriately, B/C/S, that is just the Serbian language. There is no other language in our part of the world except for the Serbian language. It is not the Croatian language. The Croatian language did exist, its traces are there to the present day but it's called the Cakavian whereas the Serbian language is the Stokavian. This is Slavic linguists. We are Serbs, all of us who speak Stokavian. The Ikavians are Slovenes, the Cakavian are Croats. In the 7th century only two clear identified Slav peoples came to the Balkans; Serbs and the Croats. There is no third group. Well, there's the Slovenians too. The Slovenes were within the greater Moravian state before the Avarians came in and then the Czechs and the Slovaks were split up too, eventually. However it is only the Serbs and the Croats that came to the Balkans. The Christian schism happened in the Serbian ethnic area in 1054. Until then, two-thirds of the Serbs belonged to the Western Roman Catholic church and one-third belonged to the Patriarchate of Constantinople, to the Eastern church. And then in the beginning of the 13th century, the Serbs established their own national church, the Serb Orthodox church and it became equal to other Orthodox churches. Then most of the Serb Catholics also joined this national church, except for the Serb Catholics on the seacoast and in the islands from northern Albania to Omis, close to Split. In this entire territory, it was Serb Catholics who lived there. When the Serbs became Turkish slaves, this happened gradually. We were defeated in the battle of Kosovo in 1389. It wasn't all of Serbia that was occupied straight away. The Turkish sultan was killed there too. The Serb state became a vassal state within the Turkish empire. That is why this taking of Serbia by the Turks was more gradual than in the case of Turkish penetration into Hungary and other European countries. The Serbs remained living in this area. As a matter of fact, they had a high agree of autonomy even once Serbia had been occupied, because the Turks in peacetime tried to portray themselves as being religiously tolerant. The Roman Catholic Church saw the collapse of the Serb state as its chance to move east, and they made every effort to Catholicise as many Serbs as possible and was assisted by Austria, Hungary, and by Venice. Whenever there was famine in Dalmatia, large quantities of wheat were brought in and Serbs were told that their children would not go hungry if they became Catholics. You would get wheat, that is what they told them. Serb literature abounds in such examples. In the Austrian Empire, a Serb could not become a high-ranking officer unless he converted to Catholicism, the same happened in the Republic of Venice. So that is how systematically, over the centuries, Serbs were Catholicised. In the beginning of the 19th century, there was no Croatian people. There was a certain autonomy in Austria, but it was reduced to three districts: Zagreb, Varazdin, Krizevci, so that is present-day Zagreb and its outskirts, but even that is not the real Croatia, the real Croatia was between Cetina, Gvozd, and Sava. Under the Turks, it collapsed, it disappeared. Croats moved to Austria, today they live in the so-called Gradiste region near Vienna. The present-day president of Slovakia is a Croat originally. There are villages where there are traces of this Croatian language and where we know that Croats moved in the 16th and 17th centuries. They moved to Europe because they fled from the Turks. As the Turks engaged in looting expeditions in those territories that they did not manage to occupy, so they looted these areas and they captured people. The Croats simply disappeared. The Croatian nobility was moved from Hungary to the area around Zagreb. The Slovenes happened to be here but then the Croatian nobility was imposed on them. People to this day speak Kajkavian to this day and they imposed the name of Croats on them, on these Slovenes. In the time of growing national awareness in Europe in the beginning of the 19th centuries, the Croats were not there. There is no Croatian movement in the first half of the 19th century. There's the Ilirian movement that was headed by Ljudevit Gaj, a German. With the assistance of the Vienna court he wanted to rally together in a single national movement as many Serbs as possible; however, the name of Serbian movement was not right because of the newly established Serbian state. So he took out of the distant past the Ilirian name although we Slavs have nothing to do with the Ilirians because the Ilirians went extinct long before Christ. So this term did not really live among the people. Their first publications came out in the Kajkavian language, that is to say in Slovenian, and it was reduced to Zagreb, Varazdin, and Krizevci, those areas. Then there was a new initiative, the Yugoslavia idea. The protagonist was Bishop Strossmayer again originally a German, on the instructions of the Austrian court. We are going to bring all Serbs together, the Orthodox and the Catholic; however, under this Yugoslav name in order to have a differentiation vis-a-vis the state of Serbia which later turned into the Kingdom of Serbia. The Croats didn't really have a real national movement in the 19th century. It's only towards the end of the 19th century that what started was a more intensive Croatisation under the leadership of the Roman Catholic clergy and the first Catholic Croatian congress was held in Zagreb in 1900. They proclaimed that all of those who speak the Serbian language and who are Catholic by religion are Croats, or rather, that in the Balkans all Catholics were Croats. That is when this artificial Croatisation started and this led to a big problem. All of this was done artificially, I explained all of this and documented all of this in my book and supported each and every one of these theses with argumentation. What should be borne in mind in this context is that the first project of the Serb lands already in 1683 was offered by Count Djordje Brankovic to the Austrian empire. This is after the great Vienna war when the Austrian army got all the way to Skopje in the south when all of Hungary was liberated. The Austrian empire agreed to that and he even appointed Count Brankovic the Serb despot. According to Byzantine tradition, it was the position of viceroy when compared to Western tradition. However, since Austria did not manage to carry through all of its ambitions and after General Piccolomini's death they had to withdraw and Djordje Brankovic was isolated in the town of Heb in the Czech lands. Arsenije Gagovic, the leader of the Piva monastery, presented to the representatives of the Russian state the project that he would call a Greater Serbia that would encompass all the Serbs in the Balkans. A similar plan was sent by the Serb metropolitan priest Stevan Stanimirovic in 1804 to the Russian empire. The Prosecution made an effort to link up Garasanin to the Nacertanije of Ilija Garasanin -- although it advocates the Serb people but it only pertains to Serb lands under Turkish occupation, whereas the project of a Greater Serbia insists on Serb territories that were under Turkey and under Austria and under Hungary and under Venetian occupation while the Republic of Venice was still there. So that's the difference. I am going to slow down again. I am being cautioned. I get carried away by telling this story, but I didn't want to write down everything that I am going to tell you about today. I thought that perhaps in this way you would be in a position to listen to me more carefully, if I tell you about this in my own words. As for the project of Greater Serbia Svetozar Miletic gave it thought; then Serb radicals in Vojvodina, Bosnia-Herzegovina, Croatia, and Slavonia; Stevan and Vladislav Kacanski published a newspaper called Velika Srbija, Greater Serbia, in the 1880s and 1890s; then Dragutin Ilic, the brother of Vojislav Ilic, one of Serbia's greatest poets published a daily newspaper, Greater Serbia, in 1903. For three years, this daily newspaper was published at the Salonika front as well in 1916 and 1917 and 1918. And in the 1920s the Serb Radical Party in Belgrade published Velika Srbija for a number of years. A Greater Serbia was also advocated by intellectuals around the Serbian Intellectual Club and also some members of the Ravna Gora movement were supporters of Greater Serbia, but this was never the official policy of the movement as a whole because the Ravna Gora movement insisted on the renewal of a comprehensive Yugoslavia and its leadership General Dragoljub Mihaljovic headed the royal army in the homeland. The people popularly called them the Chetniks, this army, because their military operations in the beginning of the Second World War were based on the Chetnik guerilla warfare. Therefore, the concept of a Greater Serbia has nothing to do with either Slobodan Milosevic or any other personage who is named in this indictment as a participant in the joint criminal enterprise linked with me. The concept of a Greater Serbia in 1990 was renewed by us as the Serb Chetnik Movement, as the Serb Radical Movement and started printing the paper Velika Srbija, Greater Serbia, and there have been 3.000 issues and it has been published for the last 17 years. It has many readers, perhaps because we hand it out free of charge to the people. I'd like to clarify one other point before the break so that I could move on to the Prosecution's pre-trial brief after the break. I have been accused of the fact that most of my crimes I carried out through hate speech. The incrimination of hate speech has no precedent in international criminal law. The Prosecution is not even able to define what hate speech actually is. The Council of Europe has been dealing with hate speech since 2001 onwards, and several recommendations were made, the essence of which is that hate speech should be avoided in the media, along with insistence that in suppressing hate speech what should not be resorted to were prison sentences for it, but other forms of ensuring that hate speech is stopped and repressed. And the construct of hate speech itself, the concept itself, is based on certain examples of the prevention of expansion of racial hatred in Anglo-Saxon law. When they attempted in England to expand the concept of racial hatred and intolerance to religious hatred they came across difficulties and the House of Lords did not pass the law project because it was considered that it was an attack on free speech. The Prosecution says that the concept of hate speech was applied in the International Court for Rwanda. Yes, it was in several judgements although I never received the judgements and they should have sent me the judgements, everything that was quoted, they should have provided me in the Serbian language so that I could deal with that, but they failed to do this. So in Rwanda, the genocide was established, and that is not challenged. 800.000 people were killed, almost an entire national group was killed. Genocide is different from any other war crime. It is different in that with genocide you have to prove the dolus specialis in other crimes you can use dolus eventualis but with genocide that is strict. You have to have the dolus specialis proved. For somebody to be accused of genocide, you must prove the genocidal intent directly, whether we're dealing with people who killed directly or who issued orders that others be killed. And people were sentenced there because they called over the radio for the killing of the Tutsis. Or for example a mayor of a town from all the Tutsis had been killed and exterminated, he incited people to these killings. And so on and so forth. So people in power who called for the liquidation of an ethnic group of its own citizens. That did not happen in the Balkans, there was none of that. There was no genocide, and you cannot ascribe to me any direct incitement to the commission of war crimes, never, nowhere. You have to incite it directly, immediately, because after the incitement you come to action. There must be action. It must be acted upon, and not several months later and several years later and so on and so forth. And the most important point is this: The genocide in Rwanda took place in 1994. So you cannot rely on the practice of the International Tribunal for Rwanda who tried war crimes that happened after my alleged crimes. The Prosecution has to refer and rely to something that happened earlier. The Prosecution cannot find an example of that. It's doing its best, it's trying to, and it refers to the Nuremberg trial. For example, in the Nuremberg trial, it was not an international trial in the proper sense, it was a military court by the victory powers, and only four powers there, Russia, or rather, the Soviet Union; America; France; and England. Some states that were participants in the anti-Hitler coalition ask that their judges take part but that was rejected. Yugoslavia also asked but its proposal was rejected. Now, of course, I say that it wasn't a court in the true sense of the word because there was no appeals. There was just the judgement and liquidation followed. However, I agree that all those convicted deserved their sentence, so from the moral standpoint these crimes were indeed proved. A man called Julius Streicher was tried, for instance, and he was the Obergruppenfuhrer of the SA, that is to say, a high-ranking functionary of the paramilitaries of the Nazi party, and he was proclaimed the number one persecutor of the Jews, the main persecutor of the Jews, and he kept calling for the liquidation of the Jews, the Holocaust. He personally took part in toppling and destroying the synagogues. He used a riding crop to beat the Jews that had been taken prisoner. He destroyed the synagogue in Nuremberg personally and was one of the main organizers of what was called Crystal Night. So Julius Streicher was not sentenced for a verbal crime, but for the extermination of the Jews when genocide was not a term in international law. The convention on genocide was enacted only after World War II, but what was spoken about at the time was the extermination of the Jews. So how can the Prosecution compare me to him? However, the Prosecution intentionally seems to be forgetting that somebody else was tried there, and that was Hans Fritzsche who was one of the main chiefs of propaganda, Goebbels's right-hand man of the German Reich. Hans Fritzsche was the head of the radio department of the Ministry of Propaganda, and he directly supervised 2.300 journalists, all the papers published in Germany at that time under the Nazi authorities was supervised by him. Hans Fritzsche after Goebbels was the principal protagonist of the Reich, and he was freed, although he advocated Reich policy in all the media and the racial policy and totalitarian policy and all the rest, the policy to conquer. How then can the Nuremberg judgement be a fulcrum point for the Prosecution? What also happened is this: A Soviet member of the International Criminal Tribunal Major Nikitchenko had as a dissenting opinion, he did not agree, he expressed his disagreement with the freeing of Fritzsche and it's very interesting to note and to look at the arguments he put forward in his dissenting opinion against the freeing of Fritzsche. American, French, and the other judge rejected these arguments and Fritzsche was acquitted. I'm not sure that I'm going to have time to go through all this and present it to you here because I would like to speak about something that I think is far more important, but if there is time left over at the end, I would like to go back to this and I have certain excerpts from the dissenting opinions and arguments put forward by Judge Nikitchenko which is three and a half pages of dense text. So I see that we're nearing the break. We've been going for an hour and a half, so I don't want that to reduce my time for other matters too much. However, as regards hate speech, I would have something to add after the break. I hope that that makes it exactly an hour and a half. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because it's a new crime just conjured up which never existed before in international customary law and it cannot exist, or rather, physical perpetration through hate speech does not exist. I'm going to quote two cases drawn from American legal practice, court practice: Brandenberg versus Ohio. The Supreme Court of the United States of America on the 9th of June, 1969, drew the following conclusion that inciting conduct contrary to the law is not a crime but direct incitement to commit a crime is and Chaplinsky versus New Hampshire says a speech which is directly or must immediately result in violence for it to be considered. Now, attempting to accuse me of using hate speech to perpetrate a crime, the representative of the indictment relies on quotations from my speeches taken out of context, and I'd like to remind you of the famous statement made by the French cardinal, Cardinal Richelieu, "Just give me one sentence," he said, "taken out of any text and I will find in its sufficient reason to send the author thereof to the guillotine." I'm paraphrasing maybe it's not word for word what the Cardinal said, but anyway. But the inciter must know the individual who he is inciting. Incitement must be premeditated. There is no chance incitement or inducement without premeditation. Now, in the indictment and in the pre-trial brief, not only do we lack a definition of hate speech, but also we lack concrete crimes committed through hate speech. Various crimes are enumerated here, perpetrated by who knows whom in who knows what location, but there's not a single crime, a single criminal act perpetrated by my hate speech which represents direct incitement to commit a crime. Furthermore, there is no objective or subjective link between the associates, accomplices. Very often there is no direct perpetrator either, despite the fact that there is no concrete incitement to a set crime, there's no assistance and help in carrying it out. There's no joint criminal enterprise, there's none of that there. And criminal law cannot be interpreted by analogy to the detriment of the accused. I now like to refer to the last portion of the pre-trial brief of the Prosecution which is a broader version of the indictment itself, I don't want to waste time looking at the indictment first and then this. So I'll go through it point by point to show you how this does not correspond to the facts, to the truth, and that it is not founded or grounded on any rightful premise. In the first point, it says that at the relevant time I was one of the most prominent politicians in the former Yugoslavia and wielded considerable political power and influence. That is absolutely untrue. My political party was not registered at all in 1990. In 1990 I was imprisoned three times for demonstrating, demonstrations, because those demonstrations and rallies were not -- did not suit the regime and for some other reasons, too, but of an exclusively political nature. Now, how someone who has no parliamentary political party can have significant political power and influence I don't know. In 1991, the Serbian Radical Party was registered; however, right up until the month of July that same year, we were a party outside parliament. At some additional elections that were held in Belgrade district at the end of June 1991 I was elected as deputy, national deputy, and throughout that same year, 1991, and throughout 1992, I was the sole deputy of the Serb Radical Party in parliament, which numbers 250 members. So my political influence and power could be expressed in the ratio of 1:250. I'm saying all this just to illustrate how much seriousness the Prosecution lacks, and this applies to me and the joint criminal enterprise. How could I have taken part in the formulation, planning, and execution of the JCE? I suppose while Milosevic held me in prison; is that it? Well, I did plan various enterprises, but none of them with him at the time. I planned toppling him from power. And had the aim been of that enterprise to expel forcibly thousands of non-Serbs from their homes, that is quite untrue. Throughout 1990, 1991, and 1992 in all my political speeches, in striving for a Greater Serbia, and mentioning the territories that Greater Serbia should comprise, I speak about brotherhood and unity of the Serbs, the Orthodox Serbs, Serb Catholics, Serb Muslims, and Serb Protestants, and that is what I was doing and am doing as a member of the opposition, not as a man belonging to the regime right up until 1988, I was never a man of the regime. It is nebulous to read in point 2 that under my leadership and the leadership of my co-perpetrators, civilian and paramilitary organs participated in the taking over of power throughout Croatia and Bosnia and Herzegovina. It means that the JNA and the army and the police were under my direction, if I had that much influence and power over the army and the police, I would have taken over power back in 1991. What would I have been waiting for? If under all that was under my direction, I wouldn't have needed elections in the first place. The secret arming of Serb civilians. Who did that? Where would I get the arms to secretly arm Serbian civilians? The proclamation of autonomous regions in Croatia and the Bosnia and Herzegovina administrative unit. The people spontaneously did that. Who would have been able to force such a mass of people to a certain political conduct if that people had not felt under threat for various reasons? When Tudjman came to power, immediately the iconography of Ustashas was renewed all over Croatia, and it was well-known, that iconography, to the Serbian people. In Croatian parliament a speaker comes to the floor and makes the Ustasha salute. In the middle of Croatian parliament. What else could Serbs expect? Back in 1941 Serbs waited to be genocide, sitting on their hands. Who could have expected Roman Catholic clerics to take up arms and start slaughtering them? Nobody could have been known that and nobody could after the Second World War, none among the Serbs could wait silently for that to happen to them again. There is a reference to the systematic cleansing of the Muslim, Croatian and other non-Serb population in Croatia and Bosnia and Herzegovina. Where was this systematic cleansing? I don't rule out the possibility that there were criminal acts of persecution in these territories, but it was a civil war. The civil war happened between Orthodox Serbs, Catholic Serbs, and Muslim Serbs and the very fact that this war happened, that fact in itself led to huge movements of population, people left to go to places where they would feel safer. Like in every civil war crimes happened, but every crime has a name, a qualification. There is not a single crime for which we would not be able to find the name of the perpetrator and the name of his accomplices on any grounds. What are the restrictive measures and discriminatory measures that I introduced in those territories against the non-Serb population and where would I have taken the power? If I didn't have power in a place, I couldn't do anything but speak. As far as my specific elements of responsibility are concerned, it is said first that I led to the perpetration of crimes by systematic and public propaganda of crimes in territories which are better known as Greater Serbia, delineated by the line Karlobag-Ogulin-Karlovac-Virovitica, and it comprised large parts of Croatia. If Yugoslavia was able to break up, it could have broken up into its integral parts, the Serb territory on the one hand and the Croat and Slovene territory on the other hand. What other territories would be involved? Why would it break up along the lines of internal borders of administrative units? Those borders were never formulated by any internal law. They were not internationally recognised. Internationally recognised borders belonged only to Yugoslavia. Those were guaranteed by the OSCE conference, and that right of Yugoslavia was trampled. It's not possible to simply promote new borders instead of those real ones, instead of the internationally recognised ones, that is contrary to the basic principles of international law. It is said that by public and systematic causing of fear among Serbs, I made Serbs believe that Serbs -- that Croats, Muslims, and other non-Serbs were their enemies, which led to violence and incitement of crimes cited in the indictment. Why would I be causing fear and hatred when all that was already happening? The very fact that the first Croatian official pronounced that Croatia would secede from Yugoslavia caused both fear and hatred. If Tudjman had not moved to secede with Croatia, there would have been no war. Tudjman said himself that there would have been no war had Croats not wanted it. That statement of Tudjman's was quoted many times. If there had been no Croatian separatism, there would have been no war. There would have been great trouble, political trouble, within the state in order to settle all the interrelationships for all interests to be satisfied, but that is a matter of political process. Those who wanted to secede with Croatia, they caused war; those who wanted to secede with Bosnia and Herzegovina, they caused war. As for the naming of Serb enemies, I was only speaking of historical facts. It is a historical fact that Croats were very pliable and susceptible to manipulation by the Roman Catholic church. In the Second World War Croats were loyal and sincere supporters of Hitler until 1943. They started turning coat only when they realised Hitler would lose the war and then they started joining partisan detachments. Very few Croats were genuine antifascists in 1941. The uprising against Hitler and his allies happened only in territories populated by Orthodox Serbs. In the Second World War, the Muslims were instrumentalised by Croats, and to a large extent they participated in Croat crimes, but not all Muslims. There were also Muslims partisans and Muslim Chetniks. There was a Chetnik Vojvoda, a Muslim, Ismet Pupovac, he had a detachment of 2.000 Muslim Chetniks, and the vice-president of the national committee of the Ravna Gora Movement of Draza Mihajlovic, was another Muslim, Mustafa Mulalic. After the war, the Communists tried him together with Draza Mijhajlovic. I only presented the historical truth; that historical truth must not be concealed. It must be repeated over and over again, it must be explained, and further researched in order to serve as a lesson for the future. Wherever historical truth is concealed, peoples and nations are condemned to having history repeat itself. By recruiting, organizing, financing, supporting, directing, encouraging, instigating Serb volunteers, that's what they say. I really organized and rallied Serb volunteers and as the president of the Serb Radical Party, I did that. The Serbian Chetnik Movement was part of the party and I did send them to the front line; they participated in the fighting. However, some things need to be clearly distinguished here. The volunteers of the Serb Radical Party were called Serb Chetniks, but they were not the only Serb Chetniks in this war. Serb opponents called all Serb enemies Chetniks. They called Chetniks members of the Serbian Renewal Party, the SDS, and God knows what other political parties. There was a huge identification of Serbs with Chetniks on a large scale. Nobody wanted to identify them with the victorious partisans from the Second World War. I can have at least moral responsibility for what might have been done by the volunteers of the Serb Radical Party during the war. Those who were rallied by the Serb Radical Party in Belgrade and who were sent by the Serb Radical Party to the front. But that formulation must be limited only to that, not to all Chetniks. Whenever somebody is named as a Chetnik somewhere, he automatically is a Seselj's man. What does that mean? After this -- after this trial is over, the Judges and everybody who works here might become Seselj's men, and I will even try to achieve that, but what does that really mean? The volunteers of the Serb Radical Party participated in the war exclusively within the units of the Yugoslav People's Army, and later the Serb army of the Republic of Serbian Krajina and the Serb army of Republika Srpska. An insignificant number was in the police of the Republic of Serbian Krajina and in the police of Republika Srpska. Only up to July 1991 the volunteers of the Serb Radical Party went to the front line in circumvention of the JNA. I’m proud of their great victory on 2 May 1991 in Borovo Selo, over the Croatian police which had launched a sudden attack on the village. Since Croatia entered the war in July 1991, nowhere was there a single volunteer of the Serb Radical Party who participated in the war outside of a JNA unit. The army designated one barracks for the volunteers of the Serb Radical Party in Bubanj Potok near Belgrade. We rallied volunteers and sent them there.
