They passed basic training there, they received uniforms. Every volunteer of the Serb Radical Party had years of service written into his military service book. Nowhere ever was there a volunteer of the Serb Radical Party identified as a direct perpetrator of a war crime, and I will show that. Never a single one. I repeat that. Now, it is also said in the pre-trial brief that I encouraged and incited and instigated volunteers and groups and individuals within the Serb forces, the Territorial Defence, the Army of Republika Srpska, the Army of the Serbian Krajina, the State Security Service, Martic's police force, militias, et cetera, and that I encouraged and incited them. To what? That I encouraged and incited them to commit crimes? How? If I encouraged them, then I encouraged them to win the war. I never encouraged anyone to commit crimes. There are abundant examples of my speeches and addresses to the troops, where I said how they should be chivalrous in the war, how they should treat prisoners, women, children, et cetera, and the Prosecution has that, I submitted it to them back in 2003, it's even translated into English, but they don't care. They could care less that they have it. It says that I coordinated the activities of volunteers and other Serb institutions who committed crimes. Now, look, the Serb Radical Party had its own Crisis Staff which was later renamed War Staff and the Prosecutor keeps referring and invoking that War Staff. What did that War Staff do? You will best know that if you look at its composition. Those were 10 to 15 men, among them four to five women, only one officer - and even he was a reserve officer, a retired pilot, Zoran Drazilovic - whereas all the other men had only completed the regular military service and none of them was commissioned. What was that War Staff able to do, to command? No. They organized the rallying of volunteers throughout Serbia, their transportation to Belgrade, to the barracks in Bubanj Potok. That War Staff made efforts to sometimes find a necessary supply of cigarettes and other supplies. That War Staff made sure that years of service are counted for every member to organize funerals, aid to the family of the fallen one, et cetera. That War Staff sometimes tried, if there were occasions of lack of discipline, to use political and moral measures to help solve problems. That War Staff did not have power. The only sanction they could mete out was to exclude the person from the Serb Radical Party; there was no other punishment available. But there were no significant breaches of discipline. We excluded that person from the Serb Radical Party, and anybody who stole something somewhere, who was a drunk, who was indisciplined would be excluded from the party and would never be able to go to a front line again as a volunteer. We were never officially informed that a serious crime had been committed, and the Prosecution has no evidence of that. Now, since the Prosecution is short of evidence for these two first years concerning specific crimes, persecution, et cetera, they introduced the case of Hrtkovci from Vojvodina into the indictment for political reasons, and they say that I publicly called for the expulsion of Croat residents from parts of Vojvodina. It didn't exactly happen that way. I did not publicly call for their expulsion. I promised their expulsion once I get to power. I promised measures of reciprocity because Tudjman had already expelled 200.000 Serbs from the territory under his control, and on behalf of my party in the election campaign I launched as one of my electoral promises the application of measures of reciprocity. If I called on someone to apply a reciprocity, I called upon the then-regime, and Milosevic's MP, MPs opposed me in parliament when I made that demand. The Prosecution would like to show here that I directly called on people to start persecuting other people. Now, that is the kind of falsifying that the Prosecution engages in. I will deal with that in greater detail later. You see on page 5 that they quote from one of my speeches, where I said what this Greater Serbia should encompass, and then they omit the unity and harmony among Serbs, Orthodox Serbs, Catholic Serbs, Muslim Serbs, and atheist Serbs, and they go on to present a bit of one of my speeches from end 1990, a warning I issued. "And as far as Croatia is concerned, we the Serb Chetniks are constantly telling the new Ustasha leader Franjo Tudjman and the new Ustasha authorities in Croatia not to play games with the Serbian people living in the area of the present improvised Croatian state community, that is, the Serb territory." That is on page 5 of the pre-trial brief of the Prosecution, I'm saying this for the interpreters because they are cautioning me for my speed. You have that in English and in French. In this way I seem to have committed yet another crime. When did that happen? In late 1990. At the end of 1990, through a single speech of mine, I made someone act in a particular way in 1991, 1992, 1993, and commit a war crime? That defies sanity. In 1990 I cautioned Tudjman not to play games with the Serb people and that we will not allow territories where the Serb people lived to secede from the mainstream, Yugoslavia. I am giving him a timely warning not to play with weapons. I want him to prevent a war. I'm warning him -- I'm even threatening him, hoping that he will give up on that idea of his. Furthermore, another speech of mine from that period of time is quoted. "The most important thing is that the Croats and Slovenes do not leave the Yugoslav Federation. First the Slovenes should leave and then those who are in authority in Belgrade will carry out an amputation along the Karlobag-Ogulin-Karlovac-Virovitica."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the interpreters please have a page reference to the text that is read out.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So we are talking about 1990. I see that it is hard to preserve Yugoslavia and then I have this clever idea. If the Slovenes and Croats have to leave, let the Slovenes leave first but there are no unresolved, unsettled matters between us. First I oppose the army intervention in Slovenia. The army intervention and bloodshed in Slovenia were caused by the then-minister of defence Veljko Kadijevic and Ante Markovic, the then-federal prime minister, a Croat, they wanted to keep Slovenia in Yugoslavia by force. I was opposed to that. As a democrat, I though that if the Slovenian people wanted to leave, that they should leave as soon as possible. However, the Western powers did not allow that, they wanted the Slovenes, and the Croats to leave together, as a package deal, in order to attain the criminal objective of Germany and Vatican that Croatia lives within the boundaries imposed by the communist regime. Now, that could not happen. If the Croats did not want to live in Yugoslavia, then only an amputation could be carried out. Amputation was not my idea. Even King Aleksandar Karadjordjevic gave thought to that in 1929. He then believed that if the Croats didn't want Yugoslavia, Yugoslavia can do without them, an amputation can be carried out. Why would this idea be illegitimate, why would this idea be a criminal one? Especially if uttered in 1990. Again a quotation of mine that I'm proud of to this day. "The Croats can, as far as we are concerned, leave Yugoslavia as they please, whenever they want." So I am not forcing Croats to leave Yugoslavia. If they want to leave," why would they keep them in Yugoslavia by force? And then I say here: "Whenever they want, but we are openly letting them know that they will not take away a foot of Serbian territory, not one piece of land where there are Serb villages, destroyed Serb churches, Serbian mass graves, Serbian camps, Serbian Jasenovac. If we allowed that, we would be unworthy of our glorious ancestors, and we would have to be ashamed in front of our descendents. The Croats can create their own state but only west of the Karlobag-Ogulin-Karlovac-Virovitica line. Everything east of that line is Serbian." That's what I think to this day. Unfortunately, we did not have the right kind of political and military leverage to achieve that because there were two great powers against us. If I were in charge of the army, I would have ordered the army to leave Slovenia on time, to withdraw from the territories of Croatia wherein Serbs did not leave, and then I would say to the Croats, If you want to go on living in Yugoslavia, we're going to build Yugoslavia together as a democratic state with full civil rights and equality of rights. If you want to secede, you can secede with that territory. What was more logical than that at that point in time? There is just one single problem. Destiny, history did not allow me to come to power on time. That is the only power -- the only problem involved. Had I come to power on time, everything would have been different. I was even persuading the Slovenians to leave as soon as possible and the Prosecutor quotes that. To you Slovenians, Serbia is a very serious unbeatable power because the Slovenes were pretending to be heroes, they said that they were warriors, whatever. They would never have had a state had Serbia not liberated them in the First World War. Before 1918 Slovenia never had statehood of its own as Slovenia. They were only Austrian dukedoms until then. You see that Serbs are still showing goodwill. After that you won't be able to. After that we are going to create Serboslavia out of Yugoslavia. I am convincing the Slovenians to leave as early as possible for a simple, rational reason. If the Slovenes leave it's going to be easier for us to agree on how Yugoslavia will remain because the political elite, the political leadership of Slovenia in the 1980s was the main disruptive factor of Yugoslavia. They wanted Yugoslavia to grow into a confederation, they wanted all sorts of things that were unacceptable. From this year, 1990, the Prosecutor gives some other quotations about my threats, about cause for punishment and so on, all of my threats are conditional, though. If such and such a thing happens, then another thing will happen. So these are words of warning, not of instigation, because if it had to do with instigation then it led to events that happened years after that or months after that. I say that quite clearly at one particular point. That is when I spoke on state television in December 1990. I explain here how Croats have to be punished from crimes from the Second World War if they opt for separatism. They should be punished in a manner in which nations and states are punished in a civilised world for crimes committed by their regimes during wars, that being the loss of territories. There are many other things I say there, but the Prosecution omits that. "We Serbs are a chivalrous people. We do not take revenge against women and children, we do not carry out genocide. We do not kill. If we take revenge, we take revenge by having our enemies lose their territories by vanquishing them in a war if they impose war on us." But we did not want that war. In 1990 and 1991 no one among the Serb people wanted war, not a single person. War is what those who wanted to secede from Yugoslavia wanted. "Now they say that I underestimated the Serb -- the Croatian people when I as I say that Franjo Tudjman nowadays has 80.000 Ustasha specials armed to the teeth. That is no force to match for us Serbs. Well, it is no match for us, no match whatsoever." Even today the Serb Krajina should be free if the Americans had not taken part in the aggression in 1995. Even now Kosovo would be under Serb control had it not been for an American aggression. Even today Bosnia-Herzegovina would have been within our joint state regardless of whether it was called a Greater Yugoslavia, Serbia, whatever, had there not been for outside interference of Americans, Germans, Vatican, and so on and so forth. Then I caution as follows: "Bosnian pan-Islamists," page 7, all of this within paragraph 7, "could the Bosnian pan-Islamists fight a war against us Serbs? Recently we told them, do not let the Muslim majority become a tool of Croatia like it did in the First World War and the Second World War. Beware and do not interfere in the Serbo-Croat conflict. If the Croats use you again Serbian revenge will be terrible and you will end up farther than Anatolia. You will not even stop there." This is a warning from 1991 when there was no war in Bosnia-Herzegovina. I am giving this warning on time, and I am saying to the Bosnian pan-Islamists, not Muslims as a whole, that they will not even stop in Anatolia. I was the first one to indicate what the danger of pan-Islamist tendencies in Bosnia-Herzegovina was as early as the beginning of the 1980s, but you will never find me anywhere humiliating the Islamic faith, underrating the Islamic faith. I am full of respect for the Islamic faith, but I am a bitter opponent to all kinds of fundamentalism. At the moment it is Islamic fundamentalism that is the most dangerous but if there were to be Christian fundamentalism somewhere I would be bitterly opposed to that too. Here I am talking about pan-Islamists, and I talk about fundamentalists and so on. Most importantly, a year before the war in Bosnia, I am warning that that war should not take place. I am acting as a peace-maker. Unfortunately, they did not listen to me. Why did they not listen to me? Not because I was powerful and strong at that time, but at that time they did not consider me to be serious enough to be listened to. They were underrating me, they were saying communist dissident, spending all this time in prison, and so on and so forth. Quite a bit of time had to go by before I became politically influential and powerful, but not then. I needed to prove myself for a long time before that happened. Then another warning. All of those who have an unclear conscience should fear us Serbs. To this day people with an unclear conscience should fear us Serbs, they have reason to fear us. We Serbs have forgotten and forgiven too much in history. We have told the Croats, should they ever again resort to genocidal activities against the Serbian people, not only shall we avenge every victim but we shall also settle scores for the victims from World War II and World War I. If we are not present in some villages or we are unable to defend them we shall take revenge wherever the Croats are the weakest. Quite simply, we speak the language of force, the language of power. It's a warning, it's not a call for the Serbs to kill Croats, I'm not saying kill women and children, kill Croats, no, it's a warning. There were even some warnings that I said by way of a joke. Once I made an interview to some newspapers saying that we have river submarines, we the Chetniks, and that we are going to take one of those and go all the way to Zagreb, but all of that was by way of a warning because of this danger against a new genocide against the Serbs. It was a very real one. All factors were on the political scene, all of those that have carried out genocide during the Second World War. The Roman Catholic Church with the same kind of policy, the Ustasha ideology, the Ustasha regime of Franjo Tudjman in Zagreb. Well, he even brought in the most hardened Ustasha émigrés as soon as he came to power in Zagreb. Susak, one of them, was his minister of defence, the leader of the Ustasha emigres in Canada. So my words were strong, but adequate in terms of the historical context in which they were uttered. It was not possible to issue a milder warning at that time because it wouldn't have had the right effect. Unfortunately, this did not have an effect either. This proved to be in vain as well. Yet again, I issue a threat. "Should they attempt a new genocide against the Serb people" - I'm referring to paragraph 8 - "we shall take revenge for each Serbian life and we shall also ask to pay up for crimes" et cetera. But I also said what our revenge would consist of. It's not that we're going to do the same things the Ustashas did to the Serbs. And I threaten, for example, “the Chetniks are going to strike at Zagreb using their full strength if there is a massacre of Serbian civilian population.” So there was this real threat against the Serbs. It is not in vain that 200.000 Serbs immediately fled from Croatia as soon as Tudjman came to power. Repressive measures against the Serbs started immediately, layouts, mistreatment, et cetera. The question in this war is who started the killing. It's the Croats who started killing the Serbs, it's the Muslims in Bosnia who started killing the Serbs. They killed a bride-groom's father before the old Serb church in Sarajevo during the wedding. A Muslim criminal walked up and killed the bride-groom's father. That is what caused bloodshed and the conflict. He remained unpunished. They only tried to bring him to court a few months ago, a year ago, I don't know exactly, and I don't think he was actually convicted. I didn't really follow the case. Every Serb move, political or military, was always provoked from the other side. Tudjman abolished the status of Serbs as a constituent people, the Serbs asked for autonomy. Tudjman wants secession from Yugoslavia, the Serbs ask to remain in Yugoslavia or to join Serbia, that's what happened in Bosnia-Herzegovina too. As the separatist moves of the Muslims and the Croats became more intensive, the Serbs made more direct moves to dissociate themselves from that kind of separatist government. When I say that "Bosnia is undoubtedly Serbian and if any Muslim fundamentalists do not like that they will have to pack their suit cases and leave on time," fundamentalists I say, never Muslims, whereas the Prosecution has in its documentation my appeal to the Serbs of the Islamic faith. It starts with the words "Brother Serbs ..." From 1990, that was published in Greater Serbia, in my books, and so on and so forth several times, where with great warmth and love I address the Muslims. And I refer to the great names of great Muslim Serbs throughout history who were aware of their ethnic identity. To this day all the noble families among the Bosnian Muslims are aware of their origins, even Alija Izetbegovic said he was a Serb in the 1950s and 1960s before the Muslim nation was invented. His origins are from the town of Sabac near Belgrade. One does not have to prove basic facts. You don't have to prove -- now you're trying to prove to me that in addition to the Serbian language, there is a Croatian language, there is a Bosnian language? That is nebulous. "The loyal population always enjoys all rights and human freedoms." Where's the problem there? Then I issue another caution. I say that the Croatian hordes are attacking Croatian villages. All this is a true. In Osijek the chief of the Croatian police was killed because he was opposed to the bestial conduct against the Serbs. They killed him too. Who was the person there, who was the main person there, Glavas or whoever? It's no longer important. That was the mood that prevailed, an atmosphere of great fear and unrest, and my threats were in the sense of warnings, cautions. Of course throughout the time - and the army didn't want to listen to me - to have the army withdraw on time from areas that were purely Croatian and Slovenian and everything would have been much better had the army withdrawn. But the generals dreamt of something else, of preserving Yugoslavia and their political power and influence. They even formed their party along those lines, the League of Communists, the Movement for Yugoslavia, the generals' party. All officers had to be members of that party. Now the Prosecution speaks about my propaganda techniques. It's all ludicrous, but as we're going to have their alleged expert witness come in already in December, then it will be a cherry on the cake to cross-examine him and to show him up as being no expert witness at all. Now, the application of national stereotypes is what I'd like to address next. It says the use of the concepts of Ustasha and Bosnian pan-Islamists. They're no stereotypes, they're not stereotypes; it's reality. The Ustasha ideology is very strong today and it will remain strong until the Roman Catholic Church leads an intensive action against the Serb people. Had we Serbs given up a hundred years ago and agreed to be Catholics, the Croats today wouldn't exist at all. So 2 or 300 years ago the Roman Catholic church sent Juraj Krizanic, a Serb of Catholic faith, to Russia. He lived in Russia and the court there for 10 or 15 years and his assignment was to make the Russian court convert to Catholicism and for the Russian church to recognise the authority of the pope of Rome and then they would enable them to have power of all the Slavs, and the Vatican was even ready to give up Poland and hand over the whole of Poland to Russia just in order to have the Russian church convert and come under its sovereignty. So these are all very serious matters. In science it has been proved, they have been proved, long since and they're not stereotypes at all. This Ustasha ideology is active today as well. It's a little more covert than it was in 1990 and 1991, but it's very strong today too. As I spent a little more time on these matters of principle, I'll have to speed up to get to the more concrete and specific issues which I'm sure you might be more interested in, but let me just mention before I do that this: The Prosecution says that in disseminating propaganda I had the help of the public information media, which was controlled by another participant in the joint criminal enterprise and that was Slobodan Milosevic, the President of Serbia, that he enabled me access to the information media. In Belgrade there's a weekly called Vreme which began to be published in the 1990s, and its journalists are CIA agents, agents of the American intelligence service and as well as some other Western intelligence services as well, and they are still published just because they are funded from Soros and from abroad and similar anti-Serb foundations. This magazine, Vreme, at the end of 1992 or 1993 published a book. One of the authors was Jasminka Milivojevic, I can't remember the other, but anyway, the book was called "The Screening of the Elections," and they performed an analysis of how far political parties were represented in that year of 1992 on our screens, and they showed that of the relevant political parties, the Serb Radical Party had the least publicity in the media, especially in the state media, the media under the control of the regime, the least. And those are exact facts. It's scholarly investigation that led to these facts. In a hostile publication published there. And the prosecution says that I basically had a privileged position in the media. So I said -- as I said, I had the least presence in the media, as did my party. But I was most effective in using the time placed at my disposal by the media. Other people didn't know how to do that, to make the best use of time, but what can I do if they don't know how to do that. Each of those leaders, the pro-Western political parties, I always beat them in a television duel. Every representative of the regime I got the better of. I was never beaten in a television duel. I have not been beaten to date. And so there you get the impression that the man is doing wonders in the media and I'm very proud of that, because my thoughts are clear, they're fairly concise, they are based on history and scholarly investigation. I am well-known for never saying stupid things. So what can I do? Nobody can match me. Djindjic, Kostunica, Tadic, or anybody else, they're just not up to me, not even up to my knees. I was blocked mostly by the regime media, it was Milosevic who blocked me in the media my access to the media the most, especially during the periods of time when I attacked him most. And I did attack him and I always attacked him when he gave way to the Western forces. He gave way to the Americans and then I get out the big guns and attack him and his party and his regime and so on. The Prosecution says that I was fully conscious of my ability to influence people through my speech. Well, of course, every politician does that, every politician tries to wield influence and influence people. The success of a politician is measured by his ability to influence people. Now, what was it that I influenced people with? By what I said. Well, you can't use empty phrases alone, because people listened to something humourous or a turn of phrase and then they've had enough. But what a politician says must be relevant, intelligent, logical, well-founded, and developed. That is the only way you can wield influence on people. Mrs. Dahl yesterday held some sort of speech here and even used some emotional notes, heart-rending stories. Can she influence people? No, she cannot. Because she wasn't convincing. She didn't seem intelligent to the broad masses of the population. The people can differentiate between who is telling the truth and who isn't, because truth comes out of someone's eyes. You can tell it in their eyes, just as you can tell somebody when they're lying by looking into their eyes. That's something you can do very frequently because a person who is lying fidgets, touches his nose, looks down. There are various forms of gesture that can tell you that a person is lying. But they don't seem to like it that I have influence over the people. I'm guilty for influencing people. Furthermore it says that I said to my volunteers that they should kill the Ustashas or Turks. They found some idiot among the witnesses, I don't know who it is yet, but perhaps we'll see him appear in court, who probably signed a statement for them to the effect that I called Muslims or referred to the Muslims as the Turks. Never in my life did I call the Bosnia-Herzegovinian Serb Muslims Turks, never ever. And there's not a single shred of evidence to prove that, except perhaps some false witness that the Prosecution might be bringing in. And if I heard any other member of my party to say Turks, and that would happen from time to time, I would put them right on that score straight away. So you have not a shred of evidence to prove that. Only somebody very primitive who knows nothing can refer to the Bosnian Muslims as Turks. It is true that at times during history they identified themselves with the Turks when the Turks ruled over Bosnia, however the Turks have not been in power in Bosnia for a long time and the Muslims have retained the Serbian language. They never managed to learn Turkish, some of them might, one or another, but they left a long time ago and their descendents live in Turkey today. But most of these people never learned Turkish and most of the Muslims have kept alive the old Serb traditions, songs, and all the rest. The Prosecution also criticises me for having not only the position of political authority but moral authority as well, that is paragraph 21 that I am referring to now. Well, I assume that somebody must be proud if they're considered to be a moral authority. Now, how did I become a moral authority in the first place? Because I didn't give way to injustice, the force of injustice, I never stole anything, did anything, did anything that was amoral, that's how you become a moral authority. You can't pretend you're a moral authority if you're not. Moral authority is something that is built up over the years and decades and I have been here in The Hague here and raised my moral authority boundlessly while here in The Hague. And today even my greatest political adversaries respect me for that, and so I'm very grateful to The Hague Prosecutors for that, for raising my moral authority which is indestructible now. And now the Prosecution says, "Seselj knew or had reason to know that his incitement and public speeches on the battleground will incite and instigate volunteers and soldiers to commit crimes." That's very shrewd at first glance on the part of the Prosecution. Well, violence there's violence in every war. By definition, war is violence. Why did not they write here to commit crimes, then that would have been clearer. Yes, I did encourage Serb soldiers on all the fronts to fight courageously and bravely, but there is not a single shred of evidence that I incited crimes, incited them to crimes, and there is a lot of proof to show that I was horrified over every crime and that I would criticise other units for having committed -- if they committed crimes, I'm not going to attack so-and-so because the Serb public opinion is full of proof now. I'm not going to shift the blame on others now and name names, people who were living or dead, except if some of them are great friends like Vuk Draskovic or Carla del Ponte in Belgrade. On the one hand, his crimes are ascribed to me and on the other hand, Vuk Draskovic seems to be Carla del Ponte's best friend. So we'll go into all those details in due course to see what the role of Carla del Ponte's role was in masking war crimes. Why she tried to mask what the Serb guards did who were sent to the front by Vuk Draskovic himself. There were no such atrocious crimes that could be ascribed to the volunteers of the Serb Radical Party and since there are no crimes on the part of our volunteers, we'll blame it on others because they're all Serb forces because I seem to be held responsible for everyone, Arkan's men, Mauzer's men, or Djindjic's men, or the Yellow Wasps, or whatever, all the formations. Furthermore, the Prosecution is going to bring forth witnesses to claim that I advocated killing all children from mixed marriages, that at a rally in Subotica I publicly said that all children from mixed marriages should be slaughtered. Well, I'm not going to defend myself from accusations like that at all. I would like you to find me guilty and then in the judgement one of the main points be that I am found guilty because I strove to have children from mixed marriages killed. 5.000 people attended that rally in Subotica and they know full well that that is just not true, as does the whole of Serbia. Well, you couldn't do me a greater service than to convict me for saying something like that when all Serbs know I didn't say anything like that nor could I ever have said something like that. So please go ahead, I invite you to convict me for that. It would be a historical service that you would be doing me. Next, it says that "many volunteers of the Serb Radical Party and Serbian Chetnik Movement were well-known criminals." Now, there's a footnote there saying witness, the code is witness. Well, why don't you list these well-known alleged criminals among the Serb Radical Party and volunteers? Name me one name. Such and such was a notorious criminal, he was in prison because of that, and then became a member of the Serbian Radical Party, go on. Nobody made a better selection of volunteers than did the Serbian Radical Party, but in our party a volunteer could be exclusively somebody who had done his military service, regular military service, with the exception of women because there are a fair number of women volunteers as well. It was only our party that we tried to check out the fact that to see whether people weren't drug addicts, alcoholics, criminals, and so on. And now you give this overall assessment of saying they were well-known criminals. Well if they're well-known criminals, give us a name. If they were well-known, then the public knows their names. That's what would make them well-known. It is a problem for the Prosecution that I attended the Sabor or Assembly of the Serbian People in Srb, where the leaders of the Serbian Democratic Party were picked on the 25th of July, 1990. That seems to be a problem for the Prosecution as well. Amazing. I'm proud of having been there. I am also being accused of forming all Serb autonomous regions here. Well, I supported the formation of the Serb autonomous regions, I'm proud of that. I'd like now, so as to have enough time, to move to specific incriminations and charges. Of course I could say a lot more today about matters of principle, the structure of the Serbian Radical Party and so on and so forth, but I'm sure I'm not going to have enough time to do all that. So I'd like to move to the charges. I think we have quite a long time to the break; is that right? Vukovar, November 1991. The volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party 14 Vukovar, that is indisputable, and the Serbian Radical Party to this day is proud of the war role. The volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party first of all fought in Borovo Selo, and the Prosecution criticises me about that. They defended Serb civilians. A truce was signed at the time, some kind of cease-fire, and a certain agreement was reached with the local Croat authorities. There were barracks set up on the roads, those barracks were dismantled --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Blockades, sorry. Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Blockades were set up and dismantled. The situation was more lax and then the Croats in buses with a lot of policemen stormed Borovo Selo and opened fire immediately. It was not the Croats who were attacked in Borovo Selo. They attacked. They died first. The first casualty fell on the Croat side which was Vojislav Milic from the surrounds of Valjevo. He was a volunteer of Dusan Silni, or rather, the White Eagles --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: On the Serb side.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was the only volunteer of Serbian Renewal. There was 16 volunteers of the Serb Radical Party, and he was found in front of the building where the volunteers were sleeping without any weapons and he was killed. The others heard the shooting, they took up arms, and they beat the Croatian policemen. 16 of them managed to beat the 100 or so policemen or however many there were because they were brave young men and I'm proud of them. It is further said that on 12 November or around that date I arrived in Vukovar to visit the volunteers and boost their morale, and that that same night a meeting was held in a house on Nova Street 81, housing the command post of the JNA and the Territorial Defence of the local Serbs. That I attended that meeting along with other leaders of the Serb Radical Party and officers of the JNA who are named, including Sljivancanin, Captain Radic, and other people. That meeting never happened. The command post of the 1st Guards Brigade was in a tent outside Vukovar, and it was there that the commander of the Guards Brigade, then Colonel Mile Mrksic organized a dinner for me when I came. At that dinner party there were his most prominent officers, Lieutenant-Colonel Panic, Chief of Staff of the 1st Guards Brigade, and he offered me his helmet as a gift because I had come with a small helmet -- in fact, it's not the helmet that was small it was my head that was big, and the helmet didn't really -- how shall I put it? It just didn't look good on my head. So Lieutenant-Colonel Panic gave me his helmet as a gift. A large number of officers attended that dinner party and this alleged meeting is a complete fabrication. They found a liar who is working for the CIA and who is claiming that he had overheard that conversation because the door was ajar and he took notes in his writing pad. Well, these are the kind of liars that the indictment relies on, and that I said some rubbish, among other things, not a single Ustasha should be allowed to leave Vukovar alive. And then the Prosecutor also incited some witnesses to say that I made a speech to the troops. I didn't make any speeches to troops, I didn't make any speeches to troops, I didn't visit any soldiers in Vukovar because it was impossible. All the groupings of more than two or three men were prohibited because the Croats were shelling with mortars all the time. There were no rallies, no speeches, nothing of the kind. I'm not really trying to respond to this allegation that I said not a single Ustasha must leave Vukovar alive. Just as you might say death to the Nazis, I -- you could say death to the Ustashas. It's not impossible that at somewhere, sometime I said something like that. It's not the same thing as saying, go on and shoot all prisoners of war. And now it is said that the volunteers of the Serb Radical Party participated in the liquidation of prisoners of war in Ovcara and in the building of Velepromet. I have statements by six bus drivers who testified that they personally took volunteers of Serb Radical Party to Serbia as soon as Vukovar was liberated. Those people were in a hurry to get home, to get a change of clothes, to have a bath, to rest. Maybe some of them were left over in Vukovar, to have a bath, to rest. Maybe some of them were left over in Vukovar. Maybe some of them remained, but if they did, they did so of their own accord. A very high profile trial is underway in Belgrade for the Ovcara case. There's only one SRS volunteer, Slobodan Katic, among them. And the trial judgement acquitted him. Look at that judgement of the Special Court in Belgrade. Now, the Prosecution goes on to say that Milan Lancuzanin, a.k.a. Kameni, Chetnik Vojvoda was convicted, yes, he was convicted, but he was the first casualty of my trial here. This pro-Western traitorous regime in Belgrade is doing the bidding of The Hague OTP to convict Milan Lancuzanin, Kameni, at any cost, although he is not responsible for any crimes. I don't know which of the other accused are really responsible and which are not. I claim that not a single SRS volunteer participated in the killings in Ovcara or Velepromet, and I assert that not even Kameni did. When I asked him several years later, he swore to me by all that was sacred to him that he didn't and I believe him, he's a very honourable man. But he was not a volunteer of the Serb Radical Party who was sent to Vukovar, he was born in Vukovar. He was the commander of the detachment of the Territorial Defence in Vukovar, Leva Supoderica, as a reserve captain first class of the JNA, and he commanded his own fellow citizens over there, whereas the commander of the Guards Brigade later decided that volunteers of the Serb Radical Party from the barracks in Bubanj Potok should be attached to that detachment, and that detachment came under the command of the 1st Guards Brigade. Well, at that time Milan Lancuzanin, Kameni, indeed joined the Serb Radical Party after having seen our volunteers and members of our party. I made him a Vojvoda because he was brave, a valiant fighter. In that order making him Vojvoda, there is no mention of anything but his bravery in combat. But he is not the man I sent from Serbia to the front, so it is pointless to talk about him. That’s what I want to say. In order for me to have at least moral responsibility for the crimes in Ovcara, you would have to prove that this was indeed done by volunteers of the Serb Radical Party. If they had returned to Serbia before the crime happened, then I have no moral responsibility either. I learned of the crime itself more than a year later, maybe even two years at the time when it happened I didn't even know. Somebody called Topola is mentioned here as participating in that crime. I don't remember that Topola man. It's not impossible that somebody with that nickname was among the volunteers, but if he had remained in Vukovar after Vukovar was liberated, he could only have done so of his own accord. And I'm not his nanny to go after him and look after him and see what he went on to do after completing his assignment in the organization of the Serb Radical Party. And the Prosecution says that I again later sent the same Topola to the war in Bosnia-Herzegovina. Well, that is not true. Anyone who was guilty of any breach of discipline in Slavonia was excluded from the Serbian Radical Party and was never sent there anywhere again, that was the case of Vojin Vuckovic, Zuca, he was undisciplined in Slavonia and he said himself that he left the Serb Radical Party, you gave me his statements, because he didn't like the policy. Of course everybody will try to find a pretext like that. Now, regarding Vocin, there were no crimes there, no crimes committed by volunteers of the Serb Radical Party. There's only one thing that was true that commander was Radovan Novacic, a good man, an honourable man who lost a leg in the war. He didn't commit any crime. The volunteers of the Serb Radical Party at the time of the alleged crimes were defending Masic, Sagovina which was the last rampart, the last route of retreat for Serb forces. 11 of our volunteers were killed in one day alone in that place. Several of them were wounded and several were captured, among them a girl Dusica Nikolic. They were taken to a Croat prison where they were tortured for months in many ways. They were really unspeakably treated, but after six months they were let go and none of them were tried. Now, some crimes certainly did happen in Western Slavonia and a crime happened in Vukovar, in Ovcara, in Velepromet. A group of officers was tried here, the so-called Vukovar troika, the commander was convicted, the commander of the Guards Brigade, Mile Mrksic. But his responsibility was not proven. Miroslav Radic was acquitted whereas Colonel Sljivancanin was convicted on a much lesser charge, not this crime in Ovcara, but mistreatment of prisoners or something. I haven't seen the judgement and I don't know the exact formulations. But that trial did not establish the key thing: Who ordered that the prisoners from the Vukovar Hospital should be turned to the civilian authorities of the Autonomous Region of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem. That order could not have been given by the commander of the Guards Brigade. It couldn't have been done by the commander of the Kragujevac Brigade either. He was the one who took over command after Vukovar was liberated. The court didn't even try to establish that, and I will tell you now. I'll give you the big secret. The crimes in Vukovar were interlinked. General Aleksandar Vasiljevic, chief of the military security service of the JNA personally came to organize that crime. Why? Because the top leadership of the JNA still believed at that time that it -- an American intervention was possible in such a form that the JNA would be called upon to restore order like it was in the puppet regime of Tito and that order would be like in Tito's Yugoslavia. In 1990, they formed their own movement, the movement for Yugoslavia. It was led by the retired General Branko Mamula. Veljko Kadijevic, Blagoje Adzic, Aleksandar Vasiljevic were the key people in that party, as well as Stevan Jerkovic who was formerly the president of that party in 1991 and so on. The army leadership and the military security service needed crimes, both on the Serbian and the Croat side in order to find a good enough excuse for army intervention that would topple both Milosevic in Belgrade and Franjo Tudjman in Zagreb. And the military security service organized parallel crimes on both sides. The military security service organized the explosion in the building of the Jewish municipality in Zagreb, and they mined the Jewish cemetery in Zagreb in order for the world public to turn against Tudjman. And on the other hand some crimes were provoked on the Serbian side as well so as to create a groundwork for a settling of scores with Serb nationalists. Aleksandar Vasiljevic in person brought White Eagles to Western Slavonia. The White Eagles were brought in circumvention of the official channels used by the volunteers of the Serb Radical Party. The Bubanj Potok barracks, official buses of the JNA, Western Slavonia. The commander of the Territorial Defence of Western Slavonia, active-duty Colonel Jovan Trbojevic. That was the official channel for sending volunteers, but Vasiljevic had his own channel. Aleksandar Vasiljevic took away from the Vukovar bank several million German marks. If it was war booty than under regulations he was duty-bound to turn it over to the so-called military service of the National Bank of Yugoslavia. He never did that. All trace of that money was lost. Aleksandar Vasiljevic had come here to testify as a public witness in the Milosevic trial. One part of his testimony was in private session, but he testified mostly in public. But the Prosecution never invited him to testify in the Vukovar troika trial. Why? Why don't they invite him to testify against me? I would relish that. They didn't because they're not interested in the truth, the Prosecution isn't. They are prosecuting me for political and other reasons. They couldn't care less who organized crimes in Ovcara and in Western Slavonia. In May 1993 there was a very, very strong possibility and threat of the military putsch. Veljko Kadijevic proved that, promoting his book in Moscow. That was confirmed by Borisav Jovic and other people, too. The mobilisation in Serbia was unsuccessful in 1991 because Milosevic was afraid of the military putsch, that's why his regime did not work to mobilise citizenry. He preferred only volunteers to go to the JNA because he knew that the military leadership cannot instrumentalise volunteers to organize a military coup, as was their ambition. The response to mobilisation in Serbia was only a couple of per cents, and in Montenegro it was 100 per cent. That was not because Serbs were cowards. It's because the regime in Serbia didn't want that mobilisation drive to be successful, and of course various political parties worked against the mobilisation for their own various interests. However, when the danger of military coup was removed in 1998, we had more than 100 per cent response to mobilisation call-up in Serbia because Serbs are a brave people, a heroic people, and they are prepared to defend their country. They were not cowards like the Prosecution wanted to present them in 1991. Aleksandar Vasiljevic was tried in Belgrade because of that scandal in Zagreb, but he received a very mild sentence and the whole thing was covered up and shoved under the rug. Those were famous scandals Opera and Labrador affairs. Those who know the military security service of the JNA know that it was much more dangerous than the State Security Service. Now, Bijeljina. There had never been any volunteers of the Serb Radical Party in Bijeljina. In the conflict between Serbs and Muslims in Bijeljina, sometime in April 1992 or maybe end March, local members of the Serb Radical Party participated, such as Mirko Blagojevic from Bijeljina. He did participate in that conflict, but he never committed a crime. And what Arkan's men did and Mauzer's men did, please don't describe that to me. Not a single volunteer of the Serb Radical Party from Serbia was sent to Bijeljina, not a single one, therefore it's out of place for me to even discuss Bijeljina. The same goes for Brcko. In the fighting for Brcko there were no volunteers of the Serb Radical Party. In places where there were many volunteers of the Serb Radical Party, it's interesting that you didn't level any charges. Skelani and other places, Niksic Heights, and others, not a single charge. But you used places, localities, where there were no volunteers from the Serb Radical Party. Then it says: "Seselj's volunteers and Arkan's Tigers." Rubbish. There was never any joint or coordinated action between our volunteers and Arkan's Tigers. The volunteers of the Serb Radical Party always had strict instructions never to mix with Arkan's men anywhere, never to mix with Yellow Wasps, with Mauzer's men, with White Eagles, with the Serb guard, and all the varieties of Red Berets. Those were the strict political instructions volunteers of the Serb Radical Party received. For what reasons? We had important reasons, but I don't want to discuss them because I'm simply not obliged. I don't owe you that. I'm talking about the charges that you levelled against me, as far as the crimes of other people are concerned, it's up to you to establish that. In Bosanski Samac there were some members of the Serb Radical Party. It is correct that Srecko Radovanovic, nicknamed Debeli, was one of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, we'll have to have a break soon. I think we have to have at least 20 minutes because of the time needed to replace the tape. After the break we'll resume at 12.40 and I believe that by quarter to 2.00 you will have had your four hours. So roughly you have an hour to finish. We'll resume in 20 minutes' time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted to ask Mr. Seselj whether he will be so kind as to finish 10 minutes or 15 minutes earlier because we have another hearing after this morning at least for two of the Judges. So if he could be so kind as to finish by 1.30, 1.35, I would be extremely grateful to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll be back in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The hearing is resumed. It is 12.40. You have the floor, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I proceed? I'm going to conclude my statement of the accused by 1.30 in order to meet the needs of Madam Lattanzi. However, I hope that some other time when I particularly care to go on for 20 minutes longer with somebody's cross-examination, that you are going to accommodate me as well. Thank you very much. I started talking about what happened in Bosanski Samac. Indeed there were a few people there who had been volunteers of the Serb Radical Party among them was Srecko Radovanovic, nicknamed Debeli. He was such a capable soldier that he even became a brigade commander or the deputy commander of the 2nd Semberija Brigade, I cannot remember exactly now. However, how did they find themselves there? After Vukovar was liberated Srecko Radovanovic was a volunteer in Slavonia. The army selected a few of the most capable volunteers and suggested to them that they go for special training. I cannot remember exactly where the training camp was. Srecko Radovanovic talked to me and asked me what I thought about that. I agree that he go for that training, and he indeed went and after this training this entire group that did not only consist of members of the Serb Radical Party was sent by JNA helicopters to Samac, that is to say that it was quite regular within the JNA. I don't know whether there were any crimes in Samac or not, but I certainly know that Srecko Radovanovic never committed a single war crime. Although I did clash with him over some other matters later on in the Serb Radical Party and he had to leave the party and so on and so forth, but at any rate he is no war criminal. Now, this Dragan Djordjevic nicknamed Crni and some others who they are I have no idea. It says here that Slobodan Miljkovic nicknamed Lugar is from the Serbian DB. I don't know about that either. I know that at one point he joined the Serb Radical Party in Kragujevac and was soon thrown out of it and later on he was killed in a clash with some member of the DB. What happened there, I really don't know and in this particular case I'm not really interested. As for Zvornik, first of all the Prosecution refers to a meeting in Zvornik in March 1992, where I allegedly made a speech saying: "Dear Chetnik brothers, especially you on the other side of the Drina, you are the bravest of all and we are going to clean up Bosnia from the infidels and we are going to show them the road, as is right." The indictment doesn't say infidels, it says pagans. First of all, I know that I have convinced you so far that I'm not capable of expressing myself in such a primitive way. My speeches are fiery, they may be war-mongering, but they're not this stupid and primitive. Even when I went to elementary school, I could not speak in such a primitive way. I mean to say infidels, pagans. First of all, I never considered the Muslims to be infidels or pagans or is that possible and am I not educated enough to know that that is impossible? Islam is a religion that is directly based on Judaism and Christianity and it recognises the Old Testament and the New Testament, and although it does not recognise Christ to be God, he is recognised as the envoy of God and he -- they even refer to the day of judgement when the dead and the living will be judged. Only a primitive person can put these words in my mouth or a Prosecutor that has no general education, no knowledge, nothing. As for pan-Islamists and fundamentalists, I wouldn't have called them pagans. I could have called them "pogani", but that's a different problem, that's the problem of your translators. From the moment when this Tribunal was founded, an enormous number of Croats found jobs here. As for the territory of the former Yugoslavia there's an enormous number of Croats employed here, a lot more than Serbs, Macedonians, Albanians, everybody else put together -- well, this is the policy of the Tribunal, it's an anti-Serb Tribunal so I'm not surprised. But there is a problem when it comes to translation. Because according to the Vienna Agreement reached in 1850 at a meeting held between Serbian and Croatian intellectuals, they accepted that Serbian was their official language, not Croatian, because their language remained neglected because they used Latin and other languages. So they took over Serbian and they immediately started spoiling Serbian with some kind of artificial words. To this day they have been inventing new words and sometimes people have to make a major effort to understand what it is they are talking about. You have detained Croats here. A few years after they leave the Hague Tribunal they cannot speak this new Croat language. In the Serbian language there is a precise difference between pagans and pogani. Pagans are polytheists, and pogan means excrement, not to use a more vulgar expression. I could have said fundamentalist filth or excrement, but I certainly would not have said pagan; I know that much. That's impossible. It is possible for the Prosecutor and it's possible for these translators who have spoiled the Serbian language and who are inventing new words every day. Volunteers of the Serb Radical Party in the beginning of April 1992 did take part in the liberation of Zvornik. Before that, Zvornik was taken by Muslim paramilitary formations. In March and April 1992, everything that was not JNA was paramilitary. The Serbs had to flee from Zvornik, and then in their counter-offensive the Serbs took Zvornik and volunteers of the Serb Radical Party took part in that under the command of the JNA. There were two groups of volunteers, one was sent from Belgrade, from this War Staff of ours, and the other group was established by our municipal committee in Loznica. And they were in Zvornik from the 8th of April until the fall of the city fortress. It was very well-fortified, it's above Zvornik, and it fell on the 23rd of April. That's when the volunteers came back and there was a small group left there to secure the front line facing Tuzla, but even that group returned in the first half of May. When the JNA withdrew from Bosnia-Herzegovina on the 19th of May, in Zvornik, there weren't any volunteers of the Serb Radical Party left at all. Volunteers only took part in combat. Volunteers of the Serb Radical Party, not in Zvornik or in other places, never had detention centres, prisoners, they did not capture anyone, keep them in custody, no one. And here it says that Serb forces including volunteers. They cannot identify the members of the Serb Radical Party as perpetrators of crimes, and then they're using the broader notion of Serb forces and they included volunteers. That is ridiculous. Volunteers of the Serb Radical Party that were sent from Belgrade were commanded by Vukovic Cele, in May he left Zvornik, the end of May 1992 he was with me in Podgorica, and he was wounded, too. There was an assassination attempt, a hand-grenade was thrown at me. One of the volunteers was there as my security detail at a rally, and he -- this particular man kicked this hand-grenade. There was this other man from Pancevo who said that he was the one who did that, but Miroslav Vukovic said that he is the one who did that, so we said, all right, it was him. He was wounded with a lot of shrapnel from that hand-grenade, but I was wounded only with one. But he was wounded in the lower part of the abdomen and the legs. I'm telling you that in May, in the second half of May, he was not in Zvornik. What happened there after that, I mean really, don't trouble me with that. We won in the battle for Zvornik. If someone violated laws after that, then that person should be tried. Strategically Zvornik was very important for Republika Srpska, and that is why we had to take Zvornik and we had to take it from the Muslim paramilitary formations. What happened after that, well, those who committed crimes are responsible, whether crimes were committed or not, that is what you have to establish, but I really don't see how you you're going to link them to me. On the basis of JCE? No way. Then the broader area of Sarajevo, basically three persons are involved, or rather, three localities. Ilijas, I am going to try to cut this as short as possible, I am going to try to be as brief as possible and as we hear Prosecution witnesses we're going to deal with that. Vasilije Vidovic, nicknamed Vaske, was a volunteer of the Serb Radical Party in Benkovac in Dalmatia in 1991. He fought heroically. When the war was over with the Vance Plan, he returned to Ilijas where he was born. It wasn't the Serb Radical Party that sent him to Ilijas. At the beginning of the war in Ilijas, a unit was established and he was the commander of that unit. The Serb Radical Party from Belgrade never sent volunteers to that unit, and during the course of the war I visited Ilijas twice. That is correct, I visited his unit too. I have such unlimited confidence in Vasilije Vidovic that after the war when the Serbs had to leave Ilijas after the Dayton accords, I brought him to Belgrade and appointed him head of my personal security detail. That is the kind of impeccable morality that this man has as far as I'm concerned. I don't believe that he never [as interpreted] committed any crimes and even if he had, what does that have to do with me? You say that he had a skull on his car. Did you establish whether it was a human skull or a plastic skull? And if it's a real skull, where was it found? It dates back to when? You're trying to say it's the skull that belonged to a Muslim person, well, then there would have to be a Muslim helmet on the bonnet of that car. Well, you kept silent about that. A blue helmet of the UN was on that car, and if Vaske Vidovic was trying to intimidate someone with that skull, it wasn't the Muslims, there weren't any around him, it was the forces of the United Nations. Now, if intimidation of UN forces is a war crime, then call that a crime too. About him committing crimes against civilians or prisoners, that is totally out of place. These are pure fabrications. As for volunteers of the Serb Radical Party in the beginning of Sarajevo, there were some in Grbavica. Volunteers came there under the command of Branislav Gavrilovic, Brne, he personally came on a JNA helicopter. The volunteers fought for Grbavica against the Serb -- against the Muslim paramilitary forces. In Hrasno, a group of prisoners was taken and that is an extension of Grbavica. There was a major danger and they would all get killed. So Gavrilovic called me in Belgrade to intervene in Pale and ask for help and I did that. You have intercepts of telephone conversations when Grbavica was reverted in Serb hands then the volunteers returned to Belgrade to Serbia and Branislav Gavrilovic, since he was born in Sarajevo, remained in his native town. After that he went to Ilidza and was within the Ilidza Brigade of the Army of Republika Srpska. You say that over there there were some four prisoners of war that he mistreated, killed. It is pointless for me to discuss that. I believe that that was not the case. And even if it was the case, so what? Why would I go into all of that? Maybe he had some personal reasons for that from before the war. Who knows what that was all about? You know, you are ascribing all sorts of things to me from here and there and everywhere and I'm supposed to go into all these things as to happened. Nothing happened as far as I'm concerned because he at that time was not a volunteer of the Serb Radical Party. Slavko Aleksic at the beginning of the war was a member of the Serbian Democratic Party and an official of that party in the Novo Sarajevo municipality. When the war broke out, he proved to be a hero, a commander. Soon he became an officer of Republika Srpska. He held the most sensitive section of the Sarajevo front, the so-called Jewish cemetery, where there was heavy fighting every day. The Serb Radical Party is proud of his valour, but he was not a volunteer who we sent from Belgrade to the front line. He's a man from Sarajevo. In 1992 he became a member of the Serb Radical Party. In his unit there weren't any volunteers from the Serb Radical Party that we had sent from Serbia. He had volunteers, but from different countries; Russians, Bulgarians, Romanians, Greeks, even a Japanese person. I personally met this Japanese man. As for all these crimes that you ascribe to Slavko Aleksic, you invented all of that, you are falsely accusing him, although I really have no reason to protect him now because when Biljana Plavsic betrayed Republika Srpska, he followed Biljana Plavsic, and that's when I stopped all contact with him. He disappointed me on a political level, but in the war he was a valiant warrior. Mostar. First of all, let's get one thing clear. In Herzegovina there were two groups of volunteers. One was in 1991 in Mostar under the command of Oliver Dennis Barrett, who's an ethnic Albanian. Mujo Bunjaku [phoen] is his real name. I didn't make him change his name. I respected him as an honourable man, but he for some reason changed his name on his own, and he took the name of the hero of this movie called "The Love Story," I think you remember that movie from the 1960s, it was a movie and a book. He was there until 1992. He was with me at the rally in Podgorica in May 1992. When this hand-grenade was thrown at me he was seriously wounded too. He had a lot of shrapnel wounds on the abdomen and on his legs. He returned to Belgrade. The commander -- it was Branislav Vakic who became commander of the voluntaries. You're not ascribing a single crime to Oliver Dennis Barrett or Vakic. You are charging people who had nothing to do with the Serb Radical Party and then you say these are my men. You are also referring to this Arsen Grahovac in the context of me, and you say that he spread the ideology of the Serb Chetnik Movement, that he had a cafe called Ravna Gora, and the volunteers of the Serb Radical Party came there. As for this Arsen Grahovac, I never saw him in my life. I never met him, but my associates studied his entire biography. He was a member of the Serb Renewal Movement and he was also a Municipal Assemblyman on manufacture of the Serb Renewal Movement. He got killed in 1993. In Nevesinje there was a considerable stronghold of the Serb Renewal Movement. They had three times more MPs than the Serb Democratic Party. You are saying here that he committed some crimes. I don't know whether he committed these crimes at all. However, as far as Ubarak and Sutina are concerned as crime sites, the OTP itself gave me documents from the cantonal court of Mostar showing that the cantonal court in Mostar issued an indictment against 30 Serbs for the crime in Ubarak and Sutina. All 30 are from Mostar, Nevesinje, or the surrounding villages. There's not a single one from Serbia. They are inventing some rally that I held in Nevesinje which actually never took place in 1991 or 1992. I never held a rally there. Then also they mentioned some Zdravko Kandic, that he commanded the volunteers of the Serb Radical Party and the Serb Chetnik Movement. I never met that man. He's a local person there. He's not a volunteer from Serbia. You interviewed him. Yesterday they tried to hand over to me four CDs with suspect interviews, including Zdravko Kandic's interview. The Prosecution knows that he's not from Serbia. The Prosecution knows that I did not send him from Serbia. What do I have to do with him then? Also as far as Teleca Lastva is concerned it has nothing to do with volunteers of the Serb Radical Party. Now I'm not going into whether crimes were committed there or not. Then Lipovaca, what does that have to do with volunteers of the Serb Radical Party? You are mentioning these people who are volunteers from Draskovic's party. Why? Because it seems that even a few babies were murdered there, and then it suits you that I should be the criminal whose volunteers killed young babies. That is how perfidious the OTP is in its endeavours. I've never heard of crimes that took place there until the indictment was amended. Finally let's look at Hrtkovci because I have a few things to say. I am going to deal with Hrtkovci very quickly. There is just one thing that is correct, that is that in the first half of 1992 I publicly said in Serbia within my election campaign that there should be retorsion. Over 200.000 refugees fled from Tudjman's regime, they came to Serbia, Serbia was in a terrible condition, these refugees had nothing to eat, they did not have a roof over their heads, this seemed to be a rational solution as far as I'm concerned, and that was therefore the stand of the Serb Radical Party in the elections that were held in 1992. However, I also made a speech in Hrtkovci on the 6th of May. We have the speech on tape. It's recorded and it was published in my books twice, once a number of years ago and now in my latest book, "The Devil's Apprentice, Pope John Paul II," and we can see that this is a speech advocating the programme. It's not true that I read out lists of names. One of our activists read out the lists of names of Croats who had left Hrtkovci for Croatia a long time ago and joined up with the Croatian National Guards of Tudjman, so that's what this list refers to. In Vojvodina there was no attack on the civilian population anywhere. There was sporadic incidents before this meeting and after the meeting. But the police investigated and threw light on those incidents during the rally. A killing did take place but it has nothing to do with this one here and you know for something to be dealt with at this Tribunal the crime must have been committed within the frameworks of an armed conflict, that's the first point; and secondly, there must be an attack, widespread or systematic. There's no attack here. That's the point, whereas incidents that take place in the streets and other public places are unavoidable when you have a large number of refugees from Croatia, Serbs that were expelled by the Tudjman regime. So what is that to do with me? I sent here a report on almost 400 pages prepared by my associates. I handed that in as a contribution to the objections to the indictment. You can study it, you need not -- a book of documents will appear recently that we prepared on that document, but the most important thing is this: That not a single Croat was deported from Serbia, nobody was expelled from Serbia. Their property was not seized. It was only Croats who left and exchanged their property with Serbs and the Roman Catholic Church always acted as mediator and no agreement was reached until the Roman Catholic Church in Vojvodina through its channels checked to see whether the Serb property was left behind in Croatia, and when they found out that the Serbs fleeing had left their property which consists of such and such, then an exchange took place and it was always the Croats that fared much better in that exchange than the Serbs did. I've already said what I think about being accused of saying that children from mixed marriages should be killed and there was another shoehorn incident mentioned, and that was brought up by Minimax a comedian, a Serb comedian in a program called Minimaxovizija. Because of the communist prejudice, part of the public thought that Serb Chetniks were traditional slaughterers, cutters of throats and that's how the communists portrayed them in World War II. In this humouristic programme, he asks me, "You Chetniks, are you still cutting throats?" And my answer was a very quick one. "Of course we slaughter but we no longer slaughter with knives, we slaughter with shoe-horns which had gone rusty, rusty shoe-horns in actual fact so you can't know whether the victims succumbed to tetanus or to throat cutting." Well, black humour, perhaps you don't like that kind of humour, I myself do, and that programme was televised two years ago when Minimax died, the comedian Minimax died, and I write about all this in my book and now the Prosecution has found a false witness who said at the rally in Subotica I said we are going to gouge Croats, their eyes, with rusty shoe-horns. When I mentioned shoe-horns, I never mentioned Croats at all in the same context. Now, gentlemen, Judges, I have a few more words to say in the 22 remaining minutes. Four years in detention for me was a systematic violation of my rights, which is so evident that it hampered the public interests and the credibility and moral and legal integrity of the International Tribunal even if it were legitimate and lawful. And it also completely jeopardized the right of that Tribunal to try me as an accused. It is quite obvious an abusive procedure which does not question authority but makes it incumbent on the Trial Chamber to exercise its discretionary right and refuse to try an accused if there has been a violation of the rights of the accused. Now, you have been almost five years too late, so it's impossible to ensure a fair trial after that passage of time, and any request to try me you as the Trial Chamber are asked to violate your own feelings and sentiments of legality and proper conduct. The violations of my rights are very serious so that you cannot keep your own integrity except by exercising your discretionary right to rescind the indictment -- dismiss the indictment. Over the past five years I have been subjected to systematic torture. Now, what did that torture consist of? As to the length of detention, a reasonable period of time was long overstepped. There's no lawyer in the world that won't confirm that that reasonable amount of time was overstepped a long time ago. On two occasions I was refused all contact with my immediate family, the first time for seven months, the second time for two months, telephone contacts and all other contacts. Four -- for four years they have tried to impose counsel upon me. First of all, that created mental disquiet and it was a costly procedure. Legal proceedings were taken with the Dutch Chamber and so on with respect to persons that wanted to be my Defence counsel. And for four years I was prevented from communicating with my legal associates in regular fashion. They also refused in the beginning to send me documents in the Serbian language and in hard copy, on paper. It took four years for them to impose electronic disclosure, and they limited the length of my motions and the Trial Chamber overstepped its authority because it is not a legal act; they can only make recommendations. So his recommendation is not the same as a Statute or Rules of Procedure and Evidence. With the mention of names of certain members of the Registry and their criminal acts, let me say that I was prevented from speaking, the floor was taken away from me, all the transcripts were redacted which is also against the law. No member of the Registry can be protected to be tried by the public. In June 2005 I was informed that an initiative was taken to establish a lack of respect of the Tribunal -- contempt of court, actually, and I don't know why that motion was set in motion because everything was done secretly. So I don't know why the Prosecutor initiated proceedings for contempt of court. At the end of 1995, the Trial Chamber issued an order to seize some of my documents which had previously been disclosed to me by the Prosecution. I don't know to the present day what the contents of those documents are, I didn't have time to read them through all, but they just stormed in with an order to seize the documents in my cell and now allegedly the Registry is storing those documents. I don't know what they're about, what they contain. Pursuant to Rule 68(i), potentially exculpatory material has not been disclosed to me. What I received was negligible compared to all the documents that the Prosecution has at their disposal in that regard. I have been forced over these five years to be witness to systematic and terrible pressure and coercion on other Hague accused to agree to plea agreement with the Prosecution and to testify against other people. There have been -- there has been a lot of false testimony. There was also some killing, and a group of officers accused of the crimes in Srebrenica, Lieutenant-Colonel Dragan Jokic was brought out although he has already been judged, he's forced -- he was forced to testify but he did not reach a plea agreement and since he refused to testify, having been under pressure, proceedings were initiated for contempt of court. They are prone to use intimidation, pressure, and other forms of method. They told people that they are potentially a suspect and that they would be indicted. Some people buckled in and agreed to testify against me, but now when the Hague Tribunal is no longer able to issue proceedings against them they refused to be false witnesses anymore. The Prosecution promised other people that if they falsely testify against me their entire families would be transferred abroad, they would get a new house, new job, money, et cetera, and they agreed. They would sell their soul to the devil and then it turned out The Hague Prosecution office cheated them, they got none of those things and now they don't want to testify anymore. Despite the decision in principle, that you, Mr. Antonetti, took as the Pre-Trial Judge, the issue of financing my Defence has not been resolved yet. Furthermore, one of the other forms of harassment and torture is the decision of the Trial Chamber to extend proceedings for contempt because of the accusations I made against the previous Prosecutor. It was said in their decision that that would be dealt with once my trial is over. It makes no sense then. That issue had to be dealt with urgently. Administratively, a large number of my submissions were returned to me because of insulting contents. I admit to some insulting things that I instructed my associates to write at the time of Van der Spoel, who the Court tried to impose on me as counsel, but this cannot be returned to me by administrative decision. The Trial Chamber has to reject my submissions, explaining their decisions and the reasons. Now, the Registry is here taking over some of the competences of the Trial Chamber. I was forbidden from mentioning any names at Status Conferences under the pretext that perhaps these people are protected witnesses, which is unbelievable nonsense. There is -- there are too many witnesses enjoying protective measures. That is inconceivable for a fair trial, for a regular trial. It is unlawful to delay the revealing of the identity of witnesses until 30 days before the beginning of the trial on the explanation that the first witness marks the beginning of the trial. The trial began yesterday. It is completely unlawful to decide that the identity of some witnesses would be revealed to me 30 days before their testimony. There is no grounds for that in the rules. The indictment against me is now reduced. Now it's not reduced. Western Slavonia, Bijeljina, Brcko, et cetera were taken out, but the Prosecution did not reduce the number of witnesses and they still intend to present crime base evidence, so I don't know whether to defend myself from that or not. And one more thing, this trial has begun without all the pre-trial procedural requirements having been met. From yesterday's opening statement of the Prosecution, it was obvious that I am being tried and the indictment against me was raised because of my nationalist ideology and that everything boils down to this nationalist ideology and the speeches I made, spreading that nationalist ideology. I am proud of that. With this false indictment, the Prosecution helped me make this ideology even more sophisticated and to use those five years to shape it even better. And I am especially grateful to the Prosecution for enabling me to suffer for my ideology. With this trial, my ideology of Serb nationalism cannot be uprooted from the Serbian people. It will grow even deeper roots. My life no longer matters. My ideology is alive and it will live for hundreds of years after my death. But in order for an ideology to be so powerful and so strong, its architect has to show, to demonstrate, his readiness to suffer for it. And I am grateful to The Hague Tribunal for giving me the opportunity to suffer for my ideology. I express my great regret that those who wrote the Statute of the ICTY did not envisage the death penalty so that proudly, with dignity, upright as my friend Saddam Hussein, I could put a final seal on my ideology. It would become immortal. Since I am deprived of that opportunity, the only thing left to me is to appeal to you to make sure that your judgement metes out the harshest possible sentence. The harsher the sentence, the stronger my ideology would be. I lived long enough, but I want immortality for my ideology. I have already made it immortal by making it ideologically sound, by grounding it firmly in historical fact, by making it anti-globalist, by being an open opponent of the planetary hegemony and dominance of the United States of America, that I am an opponent of the European Union and by being a great enemy of the NATO. That is why I am being tried in the first place and trying me is a good idea. At the end of this expose I want to remind you of one of the greatest works in literature, the novel "War and Peace" by Tolstoy, Leo Tolstoy. In one of the chapters Tolstoy describes the march of Napoleon's soldiers into Moscow and how Moscow burned and how Napoleon's soldiers arrested a group of Russian people and took them to be executed. Among those arrested Russians was Count Pierre Bezukhov with his hands tied he was going to the execution site. And at one point he started laughing out loud, a loud, sincere laugh and Count Bezukhov says: "They think they tied me up. They think they can tie and bind my mortal soul." Well, this Hague Tribunal and the Prosecution think they can convict me, that they can convict my nationalist ideology, and I have to laugh out loud, ha, ha, ha. You cannot harm my immortal soul, you cannot harm by nationalist ideology. I may die soon, but if I do, I'll die of laughter because of this ridiculous laughable indictment, the laughable Tribunal, and the laughable United States and other Western powers that stand behind this ridiculous Tribunal. Thank you for your patience in listening to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, you have completed what you had to say pursuant to Rule 94 bis.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues] ... Interpretation.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: 84, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me start again you have finished, completed your statement pursuant to Rule 84 bis. I'd like to thank you for having cut down on the time that was allotted to you. Of course if you ever need some extra time we will give you that extra time. I can only close this hearing on the conclusion you made. This Tribunal will neither convict or acquit you on the basis of an ideology, but on the basis of evidence adduced by the Prosecution who beyond all reasonable doubt will have to be confirmed. And your responsibility will be assessed against all of this evidence at the end of this trial. And you will also be providing you -- your evidence as you did and mention in the pre-trial brief. I'd like you to know that as far as I'm concerned - and I think I can speak on behalf of the rest of the Bench - you have before you three Judges that are wholly independent and that will only try you on the basis of a case file. This is what I wish to tell you. What happened before the beginning of this trial is one thing; this trial will be another. We shall meet again, as you know, on the 11th of December. The 11th of December a witness is going to come to testify, this is Witness Oberschall, who will testify for three days. We are currently looking into the exact time of the commencement of this hearing. I believe it will be in the morning, Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday, but it may happen that given that other Judges on this Bench are also sitting in other cases, we need at least one hour between one case and another. In that case, we might have to start our hearings at 8.30 in the morning but we have to deliberate on that matter. Mrs. Dahl, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Yes, we have provided notification that we will have a crime base witness available for the third day in the event that Dr. Oberschall's testimony is completed in two trial days. I think that as we get into the case we will establish a rhythm and I'll be able to predict better how long things will take, but I'm quite parsimonious in my allocation of court time and want to make sure that we have someone at the ready in case it goes faster than expected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Yes, I have one minute left before 1.30. I would like to remind you, Mrs. Dahl, that I would -- this is something I would like to impress on you. I would like you to make available to the Bench a folder, and Mr. Seselj needs to have his own folder of your documents, because the e-court system is sometimes too difficult to use for somebody representing himself, and the accused will not be able to look at the documents and check the screen at the same time. So in this binder you should provide all the documents. I also like to work on hard-copy documents. It's now 1.30, and I'd like to thank you and see you on the 11th of December.
